title: A が いちばん～ (A ga ichiban～)
short_explanation: Express the superlative degree; 'the most', 'the best', 'the least'.
long_explanation: The A が いちばん～ grammar point is used to express a superlative degree or the highest rank. It can be translated as 'the most', 'the best', or 'the least' in English. The formation is used with various adjectives and verbs, and can also be used in comparison with other items or people.
formation: Noun + が + いちばん + Adjective/Verb

examples.jp: この中で、寿司が一番好きです。
examples.romaji: Kono naka de, sushi ga ichiban suki desu.
examples.en: Of all these, I like sushi the most.
examples.promptEn: State that among all options, you like sushi the best using superlative 〜が一番

examples.jp: 彼女はクラスで一番速く泳げます。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa kurasu de ichiban hayaku oyogemasu.
examples.en: She can swim the fastest in the class.
examples.promptEn: State that she is the fastest swimmer in the class using superlative 〜が一番

examples.jp: この町では、この公園が一番きれいです。
examples.romaji: Kono machi de wa, kono kouen ga ichiban kirei desu.
examples.en: In this town, this park is the most beautiful.
examples.promptEn: State that this park is the most beautiful in this town using superlative 〜が一番

examples.jp: 飲み物の中では、紅茶が一番好きです。
examples.romaji: Nomimono no naka de wa, koucha ga ichiban suki desu.
examples.en: Among all drinks, I like tea the most.
examples.promptEn: State that of all the drinks, you like black tea the best using superlative 〜が一番

title: A。けれども、～B。(A. Keredomo,~ B.)
short_explanation: Used to express a contrast between two statements. It can be translated as 'but' or 'however'.
long_explanation: The grammar point A。けれども、～B。 is used to express a contrast or contradiction between statement A and statement B. It can be translated as 'but' or 'however' in English. けれども is a conjunction that links two clauses to show there is a conflicting or opposing idea between them.
formation: Statement A + けれども、+ Statement B

examples.jp: 今日は晴れている。けれども、寒いです。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa harete iru. Keredo mo, samui desu.
examples.en: It is sunny today. However, it is cold.
examples.promptEn: State that it's sunny today, but it's cold using contrast 〜けれども

examples.jp: 彼女はうるさい。けれども、面白いです。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa urusai. Keredo mo, omoshiroi desu.
examples.en: She is noisy. But, she is interesting.
examples.promptEn: State that she's loud, but she's fun using contrast 〜けれども

examples.jp: その映画は長かった。けれども、退屈じゃなかった。
examples.romaji: Sono eiga wa nagakatta. Keredo mo, taikutsu janakatta.
examples.en: The movie was long. But, it wasn't boring.
examples.promptEn: State that that movie was long, but it wasn't boring using contrast 〜けれども

examples.jp: 彼は運動が得意だ。けれども、勉強は苦手だ。
examples.romaji: Kare wa undou ga tokui da. Keredo mo, benkyou wa nigate da.
examples.en: He is good at sports. However, he is not good at studying.
examples.promptEn: State that he is good at sports, but he is not good at studying using contrast 〜けれども

title: A。しかし、～B。 (A. Shikashi, ~B.)
short_explanation: Expresses contrast or contradiction between two clauses; 'A, but B', 'A, however B'.
long_explanation: The grammar point A。しかし、～B。 is used to show contrast or contradiction between two clauses. It can be translated as 'A, but B' or 'A, however B' in English. しかし is placed between two sentences to indicate a contrast between them.
formation: Sentence A + しかし + Sentence B.

examples.jp: 今日は忙しい。しかし、時間があるなら、コーヒーを飲もう。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa isogashii. Shikashi, jikan ga aru nara, koohii o nomou.
examples.en: I'm busy today. However, if I have time, let's have coffee.
examples.promptEn: State that you are busy today, but if you have time, let's have some coffee using contrast 〜しかし

examples.jp: その映画は面白かった。しかし、長すぎました。
examples.romaji: Sono eiga wa omoshirokatta. Shikashi, nagasugimashita.
examples.en: The movie was interesting. But, it was too long.
examples.promptEn: State that that movie was interesting, but it was too long using contrast 〜しかし

examples.jp: 彼は疲れていた。しかし、宿題を終わらせた。
examples.romaji: Kare wa tsukareteita. Shikashi, shukudai o owaraseta.
examples.en: He was tired. However, he finished his homework.
examples.promptEn: State that he was tired, but he finished his homework using contrast 〜しかし

examples.jp: 部屋は狭いです。しかし、便利な場所にあります。
examples.romaji: Heya wa semai desu. Shikashi, benri na basho ni arimasu.
examples.en: The room is small. But, it is in a convenient location.
examples.promptEn: State that the room is small, but it's in a convenient location using contrast 〜しかし

title: A。じゃ、～B。(A. Ja, ~B.)
short_explanation: Indicates a decision or suggestion; 'well then', 'in that case', 'so'.
long_explanation: The A。じゃ、～B。grammar point is used to express a decision, suggestion, or course of action based on a given situation or information. It can be translated as 'well then', 'in that case', or 'so' in English. This grammar works with any form of sentence, whether it's a verb, noun, い-adjective, or な-adjective in both parts (A and B).
formation: A: Sentence, B: Sentence (A and B can be any sentence type)

examples.jp: 映画は時間がない。じゃ、また今度行こう。
examples.romaji: Eiga wa jikan ga nai. Ja, mata kondo ikou.
examples.en: There's no time for a movie. Well then, let's go another time.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you you don't have time for a movie. Well, let's go another time using suggestion 〜じゃ

examples.jp: お腹がすいた。じゃ、レストランに行こう。
examples.romaji: Onaka ga suita. Ja, resutoran ni ikou.
examples.en: I'm hungry. In that case, let's go to a restaurant.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you you are hungry. Well, let's go to a restaurant using suggestion 〜じゃ

examples.jp: 電車が遅れた。じゃ、バスで行こう。
examples.romaji: Densha ga okureta. Ja, basu de ikou.
examples.en: The train is late. So, let's go by bus.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you the train was delayed. Well, let's take the bus then using suggestion 〜じゃ

examples.jp: このシャツは高い。じゃ、別のを買おう。
examples.romaji: Kono shatsu wa takai. Ja, betsu no o kau.
examples.en: This shirt is expensive. Well then, let's buy a different one.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you this shirt is expensive. Well, let's buy a different one using suggestion 〜じゃ

title: A。それじゃ、～B。(A. Soreja,~B.)
short_explanation: Connect two sentences; 'A, so/in that case, B'
long_explanation: The A。それじゃ、～B。grammar point is used to connect two sentences or ideas. It translates to 'A, so/in that case, B' in English. This expression is used when the first sentence (A) creates a situation or context and the second sentence (B) indicates the consequence or response to that situation.
formation: Sentence A + 。それじゃ、 + Sentence B

examples.jp: 今日は休みです。それじゃ、映画を観に行きましょう。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa yasumi desu. Soreja, eiga wo mi ni ikimashou.
examples.en: Today is a day off. In that case, let's go watch a movie.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you you have the day off today. Well then, let's go see a movie using 〜それじゃ

examples.jp: 電気が切れた。それじゃ、ろうそくを使いましょう。
examples.romaji: Denki ga kireta. Soreja, rousoku wo tsukaimashou.
examples.en: The electricity went out. In that case, let's use candles.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you the power went out. Well then, let's use a candle using 〜それじゃ

examples.jp: レストランが混んでいます。それじゃ、別の場所で食べましょう。
examples.romaji: Resutoran ga kondeimasu. Soreja, betsu no basho de tabemashou.
examples.en: The restaurant is crowded. In that case, let's eat somewhere else.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you the restaurant is crowded. Well then, let's eat somewhere else using 〜それじゃ

examples.jp: 明日は雨が降るらしい。それじゃ、ピクニックは中止しましょう。
examples.romaji: Ashita wa ame ga furu rashii. Soreja, pikunikku wa chuushi shimashou.
examples.en: It seems it will rain tomorrow. In that case, let's cancel the picnic.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you it looks like it's going to rain tomorrow. In that case, let's cancel the picnic using 〜それじゃ

title: A。それでは、～B。(A. Soredewa,~B.)
short_explanation: Express a change in situation; 'then', 'in that case', 'so'.
long_explanation: The A。それでは、～B。grammar point is used to express a change in situation or transition from one action to another. It can be translated as 'then', 'in that case', or 'so' in English. The formation consists of two sentences or clauses, with それでは connecting them and reflecting a change based on the previous statement (A).
formation: A (Statement) + 。それでは、 + B (Follow-up action or statement)

examples.jp: 今日は休みだ。それでは、映画を見に行こう。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa yasumi da. Sore dewa, eiga wo mi ni ikou.
examples.en: Today is a day off. In that case, let's go see a movie.
examples.promptEn: State that today is a day off. Well then, let's go see a movie using change of state 〜それでは

examples.jp: このパンはもう古いです。それでは、捨てましょう。
examples.romaji: Kono pan wa mou furui desu. Sore dewa, sutemashou.
examples.en: This bread is already old. Then, let's throw it away.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you this bread is already stale. Well then, let's throw it away using change of state 〜それでは

examples.jp: 雨が降ってきた。それでは、室内で遊ぼう。
examples.romaji: Ame ga futtekita. Sore dewa, shitsunai de asobou.
examples.en: It started raining. In that case, let's play indoors.
examples.promptEn: State that it started to rain. Well then, let's play indoors using change of state 〜それでは

examples.jp: お腹が空いた。それでは、何か食べに行きましょう。
examples.romaji: Onaka ga suita. Sore dewa, nani ka tabe ni ikimashou.
examples.en: I'm hungry. So, let's go eat something.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you you are hungry. Well then, let's go get something to eat using change of state 〜それでは

title: A。 では、～B。 (A. Dewa, ~B)
short_explanation: Indicates a contrast or comparison between A and B; 'As for A, ~B'.
long_explanation: The A では、～B grammar point is used to indicate a contrast or comparison between A and B. It is used to express that 'As for A, ~ B' or 'Regarding A, ~ B'. This grammar structure is often used for contrasting or comparing different subjects/topics.
formation: Noun A + では、 + Subject + Predicate B

examples.jp: 果物では、リンゴが一番好きです。
examples.romaji: Kudamono dewa, ringo ga ichiban suki desu.
examples.en: As for fruits, apples are my favorite.
examples.promptEn: Ask whether when it comes to fruit, you like apples the best using comparative 〜では

examples.jp: スポーツでは、サッカーが一番人気です。
examples.romaji: Supōtsu dewa, sakkā ga ichiban ninki desu.
examples.en: As for sports, soccer is the most popular.
examples.promptEn: State that soccer is the most popular sport using comparative 〜では

examples.jp: 今日の天気では、雨が降りそうです。
examples.romaji: Kyou no tenki dewa, ame ga furisou desu.
examples.en: As for today's weather, it looks like it will rain.
examples.promptEn: State that given today's weather, it looks like it's going to rain using comparative 〜では

examples.jp: 料理では、和食が一番得意です。
examples.romaji: Ryouri dewa, washoku ga ichiban tokui desu.
examples.en: As for cooking, I am best at Japanese cuisine.
examples.promptEn: Ask whether when it comes to cooking, you are best at Japanese cuisine using comparative 〜では

title: A。でも、～B。(A. Demo, ~B)
short_explanation: Used to express contrast between two statements; 'A, but B', 'A, however B'.
long_explanation: The A。でも、～B。grammar point is used to express contrast or an unexpected continuation from statement A to statement B. It can be translated as 'A, but B' or 'A, however B' in English. The formation simply places でも at the beginning of the second sentence to show contrast with the first sentence.
formation: Clause A + でも + Clause B

examples.jp: 昨日は寒かった。でも、今日は暖かいです。
examples.romaji: Kinou wa samukatta. Demo, kyou wa atatakai desu.
examples.en: Yesterday was cold. But today it's warm.
examples.promptEn: State that it was cold yesterday, but today is warm using contrast 〜でも

examples.jp: 彼は忙しい。でも、友達と遊ぶ時間がある。
examples.romaji: Kare wa isogashii. Demo, tomodachi to asobu jikan ga aru.
examples.en: He is busy. However, he still has time to hang out with friends.
examples.promptEn: State that he is busy, but he has time to hang out with his friends using contrast 〜でも

examples.jp: 試験に合格した。でも、まだ勉強を続けています。
examples.romaji: Shiken ni goukaku shita. Demo, mada benkyou wo tsuzuketeimasu.
examples.en: I passed the exam. But I'm still continuing to study.
examples.promptEn: State that you passed the exam, but you are still continuing to study using contrast 〜でも

examples.jp: 彼女は有名だ。でも、とても謙虚です。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa yuumei da. Demo, totemo kenkyo desu.
examples.en: She is famous. However, she's very humble.
examples.promptEn: State that she is famous, but she is very humble using contrast 〜でも

title: Aと Bと どちら～ (A to B to dochira~)
short_explanation: Used to ask which of two alternatives is preferred or to compare two things
long_explanation: The grammar pattern Aと Bと どちら～ is used to compare two alternatives A and B, and ask which one is preferred, better, or more suitable. It can be used with verbs, adjectives, or nouns.
formation: Aと Bと どちら + Verb/Adjective/Noun

examples.jp: りんごとみかんとどちらが好きですか。
examples.romaji: Ringo to mikan to dochira ga suki desu ka?
examples.en: Which do you like, apples or oranges?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether which do you like better, apples or tangerines using comparative 〜と〜とどちら

examples.jp: 電車とバスとどちらで行くべきですか。
examples.romaji: Densha to basu to dochira de iku beki desu ka?
examples.en: Should I go by train or bus?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether should you take the train or the bus using comparative 〜と〜とどちら

examples.jp: 赤いワンピースと青いワンピースとどちらが似合うと思いますか。
examples.romaji: Akai wanpiisu to aoi wanpiisu to dochira ga niau to omoimasu ka?
examples.en: Which do you think suits me better, the red dress or the blue dress?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether which do you think looks better on you—the red dress or the blue dress using comparative 〜と〜とどちら

examples.jp: このカメラとあのカメラとどちらのほうが使いやすいですか。
examples.romaji: Kono kamera to ano kamera to dochira no hou ga tsukaiyasui desu ka?
examples.en: Which one is easier to use, this camera or that camera?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether which camera is easier to use—this one or that one using comparative 〜と〜とどちら

title: AとBと どっち〜 (A to B to docchi〜)
short_explanation: Asking which one; 'which', 'A or B'.
long_explanation: The  AとBと どっち〜 grammar point is used to ask which one to choose between two options, A and B. It can be translated as 'which', 'A or B' in English. This is often used in casual speech and can be shortened to  AかBか どっち〜.
formation: AとBと どっち + Verb, AかBか どっち + Verb

examples.jp: コーヒーと紅茶とどっちが好き？
examples.romaji: Koohii to koucha to docchi ga suki?
examples.en: Which do you like, coffee or tea?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether which do you like better, coffee or tea using 〜と〜とどっち〜

examples.jp: 映画と音楽とどっちを楽しむ？
examples.romaji: Eiga to ongaku to docchi o tanoshimu?
examples.en: Which do you enjoy, movies or music?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether which do you enjoy more, movies or music using 〜と〜とどっち〜

examples.jp: 赤いシャツと青いシャツとどっちを買う？
examples.romaji: Akai shatsu to aoi shatsu to docchi o kau?
examples.en: Which one will you buy, the red shirt or the blue shirt?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether which one should you buy, the red shirt or the blue shirt using 〜と〜とどっち〜

examples.jp: 日本語と韓国語とどっちを勉強したい？
examples.romaji: Nihongo to kankokugo to docchi o benkyou shitai?
examples.en: Which do you want to study, Japanese or Korean?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether which would you rather study, Japanese or Korean using 〜と〜とどっち〜

title: A は B が〜 (A wa B ga〜)
short_explanation: Indicates that there is something unique or different about A and describes what is special about it.
long_explanation: The A は B が〜 grammar point is used to emphasize the uniqueness or difference of 'A' by describing a characteristic or feature 'B' that is specific to 'A'. This structure is used to convey that there is something notable or special about 'A' when compared to others.
formation: A は (Topic) + B が (Characteristic/Feature) + Description/Action

examples.jp: 彼女は髪が長いです。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa kami ga nagai desu.
examples.en: What's special about her is that she has long hair.
examples.promptEn: State that she has long hair using 〜は〜が〜

examples.jp: このレストランは雰囲気が良いです。
examples.romaji: Kono resutoran wa fun'iki ga ii desu.
examples.en: What's great about this restaurant is the atmosphere.
examples.promptEn: State that this restaurant has a nice atmosphere using 〜は〜が〜

examples.jp: 私は朝ごはんが一番好きです。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa asagohan ga ichiban suki desu.
examples.en: What I like the most is breakfast.
examples.promptEn: State that you like breakfast the best using 〜は〜が〜

examples.jp: 彼は英語が得意です。
examples.romaji: Kare wa eigo ga tokui desu.
examples.en: He is particularly good at English.
examples.promptEn: State that he is good at English using 〜は〜が〜

title: A は B より～ (A wa B yori～)
short_explanation: Express a comparison between A and B; 'A is more/less than B'.
long_explanation: The A は B より grammar point is used to express a comparison between two items or subjects (A and B). It can be translated as 'A is more/less than B' in English. This structure is followed by an adjective that describes the comparison.
formation: A は B より + Adjective

examples.jp: このジュースはあのジュースより甘いです。
examples.romaji: Kono juusu wa ano juusu yori amai desu.
examples.en: This juice is sweeter than that juice.
examples.promptEn: State that this juice is sweeter than that juice using comparative 〜は〜より

examples.jp: 夏は冬より暑いです。
examples.romaji: Natsu wa fuyu yori atsui desu.
examples.en: Summer is hotter than winter.
examples.promptEn: State that summer is hotter than winter using comparative 〜は〜より

examples.jp: 彼女は私より速く走ります。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa watashi yori hayaku hashirimasu.
examples.en: She runs faster than me.
examples.promptEn: State that she runs faster than you do using comparative 〜は〜より

examples.jp: スーパーはコンビニより安いです。
examples.romaji: Suupaa wa konbini yori yasui desu.
examples.en: The supermarket is cheaper than the convenience store.
examples.promptEn: State that supermarkets are cheaper than convenience stores using comparative 〜は〜より

title: A より B のほうが～ (A yori B no hou ga ～)
short_explanation: Used to compare two items; 'B is more ～ than A'.
long_explanation: The grammar point A より B のほうが～ is used to compare two items or situations and indicate that one is more (adjective) than the other. It can be translated as 'B is more ～ than A' in English. It is used with both い-adjectives and な-adjectives.
formation: A + より + B + のほうが + Adjective

examples.jp: ピザよりハンバーガーのほうが美味しい。
examples.romaji: Piza yori hanbaagaa no hou ga oishii.
examples.en: Hamburgers are more delicious than pizza.
examples.promptEn: State that hamburgers are tastier than pizza using comparative 〜より〜のほうが

examples.jp: 夏より冬のほうが寒い。
examples.romaji: Natsu yori fuyu no hou ga samui.
examples.en: Winter is colder than summer.
examples.promptEn: State that winter is colder than summer using comparative 〜より〜のほうが

examples.jp: ここよりそこのほうが静かです。
examples.romaji: Koko yori soko no hou ga shizuka desu.
examples.en: There is quieter than here.
examples.promptEn: State that it's quieter over there than here using comparative 〜より〜のほうが

examples.jp: 車より電車のほうが速い。
examples.romaji: Kuruma yori densha no hou ga hayai.
examples.en: Trains are faster than cars.
examples.promptEn: State that trains are faster than cars using comparative 〜より〜のほうが

title: い-Adjective く + Verb (i-Adjective + ku + Verb)
short_explanation: Used to connect an い-adjective to a verb, modifying the verb (adverbial usage).
long_explanation: The い-Adjective + く + Verb grammar point transforms an い-adjective into its adverbial form, describing how the verb is performed. In English, this often corresponds to '-ly' adverbs (e.g., 'quickly', 'slowly').
formation: い-Adjective (remove い) + く + Verb

examples.jp: 彼は速く走りました。
examples.romaji: Kare wa hayaku hashirimashita.
examples.en: He ran quickly.
examples.promptEn: State that he ran fast using 〜く+Verb

examples.jp: この料理は美味しく食べました。
examples.romaji: Kono ryouri wa oishiku tabemashita.
examples.en: I enjoyed eating this dish.
examples.promptEn: State that you really enjoyed eating this dish using 〜く+Verb

examples.jp: 彼女は優しく話します。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa yasashiku hanashimasu.
examples.en: She speaks kindly.
examples.promptEn: State that she speaks gently using 〜く+Verb

examples.jp: 母は忙しく仕事をしています。
examples.romaji: Haha wa isogashiku shigoto o shite imasu.
examples.en: My mother is working busily.
examples.promptEn: State that my mother is busy working using 〜く+Verb

title: い-Adjective く します (i-Adjective ku shimasu)
short_explanation: Use an い-adjective to express 'to make' or 'to become'.
long_explanation: By adding くします to an い-adjective, you express making something (or causing something to become) the quality of that adjective. In English, this often corresponds to phrases like 'make something more ADJECTIVE.'
formation: い-Adjective (remove い) + くします

examples.jp: 部屋を明るくします。
examples.romaji: Heya o akaruku shimasu.
examples.en: I will make the room brighter.
examples.promptEn: State that you will turn on the lights in the room using change of state 〜くします

examples.jp: 友達の気分を楽しくします。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi no kibun o tanoshiku shimasu.
examples.en: I will make my friend’s mood more pleasant.
examples.promptEn: State that it will cheer up your friend using change of state 〜くします

examples.jp: 仕事が簡単になるように、やり方を早くします。
examples.romaji: Shigoto ga kantan ni naru you ni, yarikata o hayaku shimasu.
examples.en: I will make the way of doing things faster so that the work becomes easier.
examples.promptEn: State that you will speed up the process to make the work easier using change of state 〜くします

examples.jp: 食べ物を美味しくします。
examples.romaji: Tabemono o oishiku shimasu.
examples.en: I will make the food delicious.
examples.promptEn: State that it makes food taste better using change of state 〜くします

title: い-Adjective: Negative Polite Form
short_explanation: Change an い-adjective into a polite negative form with ～くないです (or ～くありません).
long_explanation: To make an い-adjective negative and polite, remove the final い and add くないです. An alternative more formal style is くありません. For example, 美味しい → 美味しくないです / 美味しくありません。
formation: い-Adjective (remove い) + くないです

examples.jp: このピザは美味しくないです。
examples.romaji: Kono piza wa oishiku nai desu.
examples.en: This pizza is not delicious.
examples.promptEn: State that this pizza isn't very good using change of state 〜:NegativePoliteForm

examples.jp: この部屋は広くないです。
examples.romaji: Kono heya wa hiroku nai desu.
examples.en: This room is not spacious.
examples.promptEn: State that this room isn't very big using change of state 〜:NegativePoliteForm

examples.jp: 彼の意見は面白くないです。
examples.romaji: Kare no iken wa omoshiroku nai desu.
examples.en: His opinion is not interesting.
examples.promptEn: State that his opinion isn't interesting using change of state 〜:NegativePoliteForm

examples.jp: その映画は楽しくありません。
examples.romaji: Sono eiga wa tanoshiku arimasen.
examples.en: That movie is not enjoyable.
examples.promptEn: State that that movie isn't fun using change of state 〜:NegativePoliteForm

title: い-Adjective て (i-Adjective + te~)
short_explanation: Used to connect two or more い-adjectives to describe something.
long_explanation: The い-Adjective て form is used to connect two or more い-adjectives when listing attributes of something or someone. To form it, replace the final い with くて. For example, かわいい → かわいくて, おいしい → おいしくて.
formation: い-Adjective (remove い) + くて + い-Adjective

examples.jp: このリンゴは甘くて美味しいです。
examples.romaji: Kono ringo wa amakute oishii desu.
examples.en: This apple is sweet and delicious.
examples.promptEn: State that this apple is sweet and delicious using 〜て

examples.jp: 彼女は優しくてかわいいです。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa yasashikute kawaii desu.
examples.en: She is kind and cute.
examples.promptEn: State that she is kind and cute using 〜て

examples.jp: 映画は面白くて感動的でした。
examples.romaji: Eiga wa omoshirokute kandouteki deshita.
examples.en: The movie was interesting and moving.
examples.promptEn: State that the movie was interesting and moving using 〜て

examples.jp: この部屋は広くて明るいです。
examples.romaji: Kono heya wa hirokute akarui desu.
examples.en: This room is spacious and bright.
examples.promptEn: State that this room is spacious and bright using 〜て

title: な-Adjective に + Verb
short_explanation: Turn a な-adjective into an adverb by adding に.
long_explanation: To make a な-adjective modify a verb, remove the な and add に. This form describes how an action is performed. For instance, 静か（な） → 静かに, 親切（な） → 親切に.
formation: な-Adjective (remove な) + に + Verb

examples.jp: 彼は静かに話す。
examples.romaji: Kare wa shizuka ni hanasu.
examples.en: He speaks quietly.
examples.promptEn: State that he speaks quietly using 〜に+Verb

examples.jp: 部屋をきれいに掃除した。
examples.romaji: Heya o kirei ni souji shita.
examples.en: I cleaned the room neatly.
examples.promptEn: State that you cleaned the room thoroughly using 〜に+Verb

examples.jp: 彼女は元気に働いています。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa genki ni hataraite imasu.
examples.en: She works energetically.
examples.promptEn: State that she is working energetically using 〜に+Verb

examples.jp: 先生は親切に説明してくれる。
examples.romaji: Sensei wa shinsetsu ni setsumei shite kureru.
examples.en: The teacher explains kindly.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to the teacher explains it kindly using 〜に+Verb

title: な-Adjective で～ (na-Adjective de~)
short_explanation: Usage of で to connect or add information with a な-adjective.
long_explanation: Use な-adjective + で to connect it to another quality, action, or description. It can combine a な-adjective with another adjective, verb, or clause.
formation: な-Adjective + で

examples.jp: 彼は綺麗で優しい女性が好きです。
examples.romaji: Kare wa kirei de yasashii josei ga suki desu.
examples.en: He likes women who are beautiful and kind.
examples.promptEn: State that he likes beautiful, kind women using 〜で

examples.jp: この料理は健康的で、元気な気分になります。
examples.romaji: Kono ryouri wa kenkouteki de, genki na kibun ni narimasu.
examples.en: This dish is healthy and makes you feel energetic.
examples.promptEn: State that this dish is healthy and makes you feel energetic using 〜で

examples.jp: 彼は静かで落ち着いた環境で仕事をしたい。
examples.romaji: Kare wa shizuka de ochitsuita kankyou de shigoto o shitai.
examples.en: He wants to work in a quiet and calm environment.
examples.promptEn: State that he wants to work in a quiet and calm environment using 〜で

examples.jp: この部屋は清潔で気持ちがいいです。
examples.romaji: Kono heya wa seiketsu de kimochi ga ii desu.
examples.en: This room is clean and feels good.
examples.promptEn: State that this room is clean and pleasant using 〜で

title: な-Adjective に します (na-Adjective ni shimasu)
short_explanation: Expressing a decision or preference with a な-adjective.
long_explanation: The な-adjective に します pattern is used to express a decision or choice based on a な-adjective. It often translates as 'I’ll make it ...,' 'I will choose ...,' or 'I’ve decided on ...'.
formation: な-Adjective + に + します

examples.jp: 静かにします。
examples.romaji: Shizuka ni shimasu.
examples.en: I will be quiet.
examples.promptEn: State that you will be quiet using 〜にします

examples.jp: 部屋をきれいにします。
examples.romaji: Heya o kirei ni shimasu.
examples.en: I will make the room clean.
examples.promptEn: State that you will clean the room using 〜にします

examples.jp: 明日の会議は簡単にします。
examples.romaji: Ashita no kaigi wa kantan ni shimasu.
examples.en: I will make tomorrow’s meeting simple.
examples.promptEn: State that you will keep tomorrow's meeting brief using 〜にします

examples.jp: 健康的な食事にします。
examples.romaji: Kenkou-teki na shokuji ni shimasu.
examples.en: I will choose a healthy meal.
examples.promptEn: State that you will eat a healthy meal using 〜にします

title: な-Adjective に なります (na-Adjective ni narimasu)
short_explanation: Express a change or transformation into a state described by the な-adjective.
long_explanation: The な-Adjective + に + なります grammar point is used to express a change or transformation into the state described by the な-adjective. It translates to 'become' or 'turn into' along with the meaning of the な-adjective.
formation: な-Adjective (remove な) + に + なります

examples.jp: この部屋は静かになります。
examples.romaji: Kono heya wa shizuka ni narimasu.
examples.en: This room becomes quiet.
examples.promptEn: State that this room will be quiet using change of state 〜になります

examples.jp: 彼女はきれいになります。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa kirei ni narimasu.
examples.en: She becomes beautiful.
examples.promptEn: State that she will become beautiful using change of state 〜になります

examples.jp: 彼は元気になります。
examples.romaji: Kare wa genki ni narimasu.
examples.en: He becomes energetic.
examples.promptEn: State that he'll get better using change of state 〜になります

examples.jp: 町はにぎやかになります。
examples.romaji: Machi wa nigiyaka ni narimasu.
examples.en: The town becomes lively.
examples.promptEn: State that the town will become lively using change of state 〜になります

title: Noun か Noun か～ (Noun ka Noun ka～)
short_explanation: Expresses choice or alternatives; 'either', 'or'.
long_explanation: The Noun か Noun か～ grammar point is used to present two or more alternatives for a choice. It can be translated to 'either', 'or' in English. It is formed by placing the particle か in between two nouns or noun phrases.
formation: Noun1 + か + Noun2 + か～

examples.jp: 今日、映画を見るか、散歩するかどちらにしますか？
examples.romaji: Kyou, eiga wo miru ka, sanpo suru ka dochira ni shimasu ka?
examples.en: Will we watch a movie or go for a walk today?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether shall you watch a movie or go for a walk today using 〜かNounか

examples.jp: コーヒーか紅茶か、一つだけ選んでください。
examples.romaji: Koohii ka koucha ka, hitotsu dake erande kudasai.
examples.en: Please choose only one, either coffee or tea.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to choose only one: coffee or tea using 〜かNounか

examples.jp: 電車かバスを使って、学校に行くつもりです。
examples.romaji: Densha ka basu o tsukatte, gakkou ni iku tsumori desu.
examples.en: I plan to go to school using either the train or the bus.
examples.promptEn: State that you plan to take the train or bus to school using 〜かNounか

examples.jp: 週末は山に登るか海に行くか、まだ決めていません。
examples.romaji: Shuumatsu wa yama ni noboru ka umi ni iku ka, mada kimete imasen.
examples.en: I haven't decided whether to climb the mountain or go to the beach this weekend.
examples.promptEn: State that you haven't decided yet whether to go hiking or to the beach this weekend using 〜かNounか

title: Noun が できます (Noun ga dekimasu)
short_explanation: Express the ability to do something.
long_explanation: The Noun が できます grammar point is used to express the ability to do something. In this grammar pattern, the noun is the activity that the speaker or subject can do. It translates as 'can do' or 'able to do' in English.
formation: Noun + が + できます

examples.jp: 英語ができます。
examples.romaji: Eigo ga dekimasu.
examples.en: I can speak English.
examples.promptEn: State that you can speak English using 〜ができます

examples.jp: 料理ができます。
examples.romaji: Ryouri ga dekimasu.
examples.en: I can cook.
examples.promptEn: State that you can cook using 〜ができます

examples.jp: 彼は泳ぎができます。
examples.romaji: Kare wa oyogi ga dekimasu.
examples.en: He can swim.
examples.promptEn: State that he can swim using 〜ができます

examples.jp: 彼女はピアノができます。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa piano ga dekimasu.
examples.en: She can play the piano.
examples.promptEn: State that she can play the piano using 〜ができます

title: Noun がほしいです (〜ga hoshii desu)
short_explanation: Express a desire or wanting something; 'I want', 'I would like'.
long_explanation: The がほしいです grammar point is used to express a desire or the act of wanting something in polite form. It can be translated as 'I want' or 'I would like' in English. It is used with a noun and the particle が.
formation: Noun + が + ほしいです

examples.jp: 新しい車がほしいです。
examples.romaji: Atarashii kuruma ga hoshii desu.
examples.en: I want a new car.
examples.promptEn: State that you want a new car using desire 〜がほしいです

examples.jp: コーヒーがほしいです。
examples.romaji: Koohii ga hoshii desu.
examples.en: I would like some coffee.
examples.promptEn: State that you want some coffee using desire 〜がほしいです

examples.jp: 彼女は花がほしいです。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa hana ga hoshii desu.
examples.en: She wants flowers.
examples.promptEn: State that she wants flowers using desire 〜がほしいです

examples.jp: 友達がほしいです。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ga hoshii desu.
examples.en: I want a friend.
examples.promptEn: State that you want to make friends using desire 〜がほしいです

title: Noun から Noun まで (Noun kara Noun made)
short_explanation: Expresses a range; 'from...to', 'between...and'.
long_explanation: The から...まで grammar point is used to express a range between two nouns, indicating the starting point and ending point of an action, event, or period of time. It can be translated as 'from...to' or 'between...and' in English.
formation: Noun1 + から + Noun2 + まで

examples.jp: 朝9時から午後5時まで働きます。
examples.romaji: Asa ku-ji kara gogo go-ji made hatarakimasu.
examples.en: I work from 9 AM to 5 PM.
examples.promptEn: State that you work from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m using reason 〜からNounまで

examples.jp: 東京から大阪まで電車で行く。
examples.romaji: Toukyou kara Osaka made densha de iku.
examples.en: I will go by train from Tokyo to Osaka.
examples.promptEn: State that you are taking the train from Tokyo to Osaka using reason 〜からNounまで

examples.jp: 地下鉄は午前6時から深夜まで運行しています。
examples.romaji: Chikatetsu wa gozen roku-ji kara shin'ya made unkou shite imasu.
examples.en: The subway runs from 6 AM until midnight.
examples.promptEn: State that the subway runs from 6:00 a.m. until late at night using reason 〜からNounまで

examples.jp: 月曜日から金曜日まで学校に通います。
examples.romaji: Getsuyoubi kara Kinyoubi made gakkou ni kayoimasu.
examples.en: I attend school from Monday to Friday.
examples.promptEn: State that you go to school from Monday through Friday using reason 〜からNounまで

title: Noun くらい～ (Noun kurai～)
short_explanation: Express the extent or degree of something; 'about', 'approximately', 'at least'.
long_explanation: The くらい grammar point is used with a noun to express the extent or degree of something, meaning 'about', 'approximately', or 'at least' in English. It helps to provide a rough estimate or minimum standard to the noun it is attached to.
formation: Noun + くらい

examples.jp: この本は三百ページくらいあります。
examples.romaji: Kono hon wa sanbyaku peeji kurai arimasu.
examples.en: This book has about 300 pages.
examples.promptEn: State that this book is about 300 pages long using 〜くらい

examples.jp: 彼の家まで歩いて20分くらいかかります。
examples.romaji: Kare no ie made aruite nijuppun kurai kakarimasu.
examples.en: It takes about 20 minutes to walk to his house.
examples.promptEn: State that it takes about 20 minutes to walk to his house using 〜くらい

examples.jp: 明日は暑くて、30度くらいになるでしょう。
examples.romaji: Ashita wa atsukute, sanjuu-do kurai ni naru deshou.
examples.en: Tomorrow will be hot, about 30 degrees.
examples.promptEn: State that it will be hot tomorrow, reaching around 30 degrees using 〜くらい

examples.jp: この料理を作るのに、材料は500円くらい必要です。
examples.romaji: Kono ryouri o tsukuru no ni, zairyou wa gohyaku-en kurai hitsuyou desu.
examples.en: You need about 500 yen worth of ingredients to make this dish.
examples.promptEn: State that you'll need about 500 yen worth of ingredients to make this dish using 〜くらい

title: Noun ぐらい～ (Noun gurai～)
short_explanation: Express an approximate amount or degree; 'about', 'approximately'.
long_explanation: The ぐらい grammar point is used with nouns to express an approximate amount or degree. It is often translated as 'about', 'approximately', or 'around' in English. This can be used for time, quantity, or other measurements.
formation: Noun + ぐらい

examples.jp: 一日中勉強したので、１０時間ぐらい勉強しました。

examples.en: I studied all day, so I studied for about 10 hours.
examples.promptEn: State that you studied all day, so you studied for about 10 hours using 〜ぐらい

examples.jp: この本は１００ページぐらいある。
examples.romaji: Kono hon wa hyaku peeji gurai aru.
examples.en: This book has about 100 pages.
examples.promptEn: State that this book is about 100 pages long using 〜ぐらい

examples.jp: 彼は果物を５個ぐらい食べました。
examples.romaji: Kare wa kudamono o go-ko gurai tabemashita.
examples.en: He ate about 5 pieces of fruit.
examples.promptEn: State that he ate about five pieces of fruit using 〜ぐらい

examples.jp: 駅から家まで歩いて２０分ぐらいかかります。
examples.romaji: Eki kara ie made aruite nijuppun gurai kakarimasu.

examples.promptEn: State that it takes about 20 minutes to walk from the station to your house using 〜ぐらい

title: Noun ごろ～ (Noun + goro～)
short_explanation: Expresses 'around' or 'about' a certain time or age.
long_explanation: The ごろ grammar point is used to indicate 'around' or 'about' a certain time or age. It is commonly used with time-related expressions and age-related expressions to give an approximate time or age.
formation: Noun + ごろ

examples.jp: 昼ごろに電話してください。
examples.romaji: Hiru goro ni denwa shite kudasai.
examples.en: Please call me around noon.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to call you around noon using desire 〜ごろ

examples.jp: 彼は10歳ごろに日本に来ました。
examples.romaji: Kare wa juu-sai goro ni Nihon ni kimashita.
examples.en: He came to Japan around the age of 10.
examples.promptEn: State that he came to Japan when he was about 10 years old using desire 〜ごろ

examples.jp: 午後３時ごろに会いましょう。
examples.romaji: Gogo san-ji goro ni aimashou.

title: Noun だけ〜 (〜dake)
short_explanation: Indicates 'only', 'just', or 'merely'.
long_explanation: The Noun だけ grammar point is used to emphasize the idea of 'only', 'just', or 'merely' in a sentence. It can be attached to nouns, verbs, い-adjectives, and な-adjectives to show this emphasis. This grammar point is commonly used in both spoken and written Japanese.
formation: Noun + だけ, Verb-casual + だけ, い-Adjective + だけ, な-Adjective-な + だけ

examples.jp: コーヒーだけ飲んで、帰りました。

examples.jp: この本は二十ページだけ読んだ。

examples.jp: 彼女はとても速いですが、走るだけでなく、考えるのも速いです。

examples.promptEn: State that she is very fast—not only when she runs, but also when she thinks using limitation 〜だけ〜

examples.jp: この部屋は寝るだけの場所です。

examples.en: This room is a place only for sleeping.
examples.promptEn: State that this room is just for sleeping using limitation 〜だけ〜

title: Nounで～ (Noun de ~)
short_explanation: Indicate a place or means for an action or situation; 'at, in, on', 'using', or 'by means of'.
long_explanation: The で grammar point is used to indicate a location, method, or tool for doing an action or for being in a situation. It can be translated as 'at, in, on', 'using', or 'by means of' in English. Nounで is formed by adding で after a noun.

examples.jp: バスで学校に行きます。

examples.jp: 英語で話しましょう。
examples.romaji: Eigo de hanashimashou.
examples.en: Let's talk in English.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you speak in English using 〜で

title: Noun と～ (Noun to～)
short_explanation: Express 'with', 'and' or 'together with' when connecting nouns.
long_explanation: The Noun と grammar point is used to express a connection between two or more nouns, indicating 'with', 'and', or 'together with' in English. It functions as a particle that is used to simply list multiple items or express companionship.
formation: Noun1 + と + Noun2

examples.jp: リンゴとバナナを買いました。

examples.jp: 友達と映画を見に行きます。

examples.jp: 彼と彼女は結婚しました。

examples.en: He and she got married.

title: Noun に～ (Noun ni～)
short_explanation: Express a specific direction, target or purpose; 'to', 'toward', 'for'.
long_explanation: The 'Noun に' grammar point is used to express a specific direction, target, or purpose in relation to a noun. It can be translated as 'to', 'toward', or 'for' in English. The に particle is added directly after the noun which indicates direction, target or purpose.
formation: Noun + に

examples.jp: 彼女にプレゼントをあげました。

examples.en: I gave a present to her.
examples.promptEn: State that you gave her a present using purpose 〜に

examples.jp: 日本に行きます。
examples.romaji: Nihon ni ikimasu.
examples.en: I am going to Japan.
examples.promptEn: State that you are going to Japan using purpose 〜に

examples.jp: 6時に集合しましょう。

examples.en: Let's meet at 6 o'clock.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you meet at 6 o'clock using purpose 〜に

examples.jp: 友達に手紙を書きます。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ni tegami wo kakimasu.
examples.en: I will write a letter to my friend.
examples.promptEn: State that you are writing a letter to a friend using purpose 〜に

title: Noun に 帰ります (Noun ni kaerimasu)
short_explanation: Express going back or returning to a place: 'to return to', 'to go back to'.
long_explanation: The grammar point 'Noun に 帰ります' is used to express physically going back or returning to a specific place. It can be translated as 'to go back to' or 'to return to' in English. The particle に indicates the destination of the return.
formation: Noun + に + 帰ります

examples.jp: 夏休みが終わったら、学校に帰ります。

examples.promptEn: Ask whether when summer vacation is over, you will go back to school using 〜に帰ります

examples.jp: 買い物を終えたら、家に帰ります。
examples.romaji: Kaimono o oetara, ie ni kaerimasu.
examples.en: After finishing shopping, I will go back home.
examples.promptEn: Ask whether when you are done shopping, you will go home using 〜に帰ります

examples.jp: 今週末、実家に帰ります。
examples.romaji: Konshuumatsu, jikka ni kaerimasu.
examples.en: I'm going back to my parents' home this weekend.

examples.jp: 友達と旅行に行ったあと、東京に帰ります。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi to ryokou ni itta ato, Toukyou ni kaerimasu.
examples.en: After traveling with my friend, I'll return to Tokyo.
examples.promptEn: State that after traveling with your friends, you will return to Tokyo using 〜に帰ります

title: Noun に します (Noun ni shimasu)
short_explanation: Express a choice or decision; 'choose', 'decide on'.
long_explanation: The に します grammar point is used to express making a choice or decision. It can be translated as 'choose' or 'decide on' in English. It is often used in situations where someone has to make a selection or decide on something, such as ordering food at a restaurant or deciding on a vacation destination.
formation: Noun + に します

examples.jp: 今日の昼ご飯は寿司にします。
examples.romaji: Kyou no hirugohan wa sushi ni shimasu.
examples.en: I'll choose sushi for today's lunch.
examples.promptEn: State that you are going to have sushi for lunch today using 〜にします

examples.jp: この靴を買うか迷っていますが、赤い色の方にします。
examples.romaji: Kono kutsu wo kau ka mayotteimasu ga, akai iro no hou ni shimasu.
examples.en: I was hesitating about which shoes to buy, but I'll go with the red ones.
examples.promptEn: State that you are debating whether to buy these shoes, but you will go with the red ones using 〜にします

examples.jp: 休みの日に何をするか決めた。映画館に行くことにします。
examples.romaji: Yasumi no hi ni nani wo suru ka kimeta. Eigakan ni iku koto ni shimasu.
examples.en: I've decided what to do on my day off. I'll go to the movie theater.
examples.promptEn: State that you have decided what to do on your day off. you are going to the movie theater using 〜にします

examples.jp: フランス語とスペイン語のどちらを勉強するか悩んだが、フランス語にします。
examples.romaji: Furansugo to Supeingo no dochira wo benkyou suru ka nayanda ga, Furansugo ni shimasu.
examples.en: I was torn between studying French and Spanish, but I decided on French.
examples.promptEn: State that you was torn between studying French and Spanish, but you have decided on French using 〜にします

title: Noun に なります (Noun ni narimasu)
short_explanation: Expresses change or becoming something; 'to become', 'to turn into', 'to be'.
long_explanation: The grammar point Noun に なります is used to express a change or transformation into something else, or to indicate that something 'becomes', 'turns into', or simply 'is' something. It is commonly used with nouns.
formation: Noun + に + なります

examples.jp: 彼は医者になります。
examples.romaji: Kare wa isha ni narimasu.
examples.en: He will become a doctor.
examples.promptEn: State that he is going to become a doctor using change of state 〜になります

examples.jp: この茶色の葉が赤になります。
examples.romaji: Kono chairo no ha ga aka ni narimasu.
examples.en: These brown leaves will turn red.
examples.promptEn: State that this brown leaf will turn red using change of state 〜になります

examples.jp: 料理が冷めたら、美味しくなくなります。
examples.romaji: Ryouri ga sametara, oishikunaku narimasu.
examples.en: When the dish cools down, it becomes less delicious.
examples.promptEn: State that if the food gets cold, it won't taste as good using change of state 〜になります

examples.jp: 来年、東京オリンピックになります。
examples.romaji: Rainen, Toukyou Orinpikku ni narimasu.
examples.en: Next year, it will be the Tokyo Olympics.
examples.promptEn: State that the Tokyo Olympics will be held next year using change of state 〜になります

title: Noun に 来ます (Noun ni kimasu)
short_explanation: Used to express coming to a place.
long_explanation: The grammar point Noun に 来ます is used to indicate that someone or something comes to a specific place. The noun before に indicates the destination or place, while the verb 来ます expresses the action of coming. (Similarly, 'Noun に 行きます' means 'go to [Noun],' and 'Noun に 帰ります' means 'return to [Noun].')
formation: Noun + に + 来ます (kimasu)

examples.jp: 友達が私の家に来ます。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ga watashi no ie ni kimasu.
examples.en: My friend will come to my house.
examples.promptEn: State that my friend is coming over to your house using 〜に来ます

examples.jp: 今晩、父が駅に迎えに来ます。
examples.romaji: Konban, chichi ga eki ni mukae ni kimasu.
examples.en: Tonight, my father will come to pick me up at the station.
examples.promptEn: State that my father is coming to pick you up at the station tonight using 〜に来ます

examples.jp: 明日、先生が学校に来ます。
examples.romaji: Ashita, sensei ga gakkou ni kimasu.
examples.en: Tomorrow, the teacher will come to school.
examples.promptEn: State that the teacher is coming to school tomorrow using 〜に来ます

examples.jp: 有名な歌手がこの街に来ます。
examples.romaji: Yuumei na kashu ga kono machi ni kimasu.
examples.en: A famous singer will come to this town.
examples.promptEn: State that a famous singer is coming to this city using 〜に来ます

title: Noun に 行きます (Noun ni ikimasu)
short_explanation: Used to express going to a location.
long_explanation: The Noun に 行きます grammar point is used to express going to a specific location. This structure requires a noun (indicating the destination) followed by に and the verb 行きます, which means 'to go'.
formation: Noun + に + 行きます

examples.jp: 学校に行きます。
examples.romaji: Gakkou ni ikimasu.
examples.en: I will go to school.
examples.promptEn: State that you are going to school using 〜に行きます

examples.jp: 明日、スーパーに行きます。
examples.romaji: Ashita, suupaa ni ikimasu.
examples.en: I will go to the supermarket tomorrow.
examples.promptEn: State that you are going to the supermarket tomorrow using 〜に行きます

examples.jp: 週末に映画館に行きます。
examples.romaji: Shuumatsu ni eigakan ni ikimasu.
examples.en: I will go to the movie theater on the weekend.
examples.promptEn: State that you are going to the movies this weekend using 〜に行きます

examples.jp: 夏休みに海に行きます。
examples.romaji: Natsu yasumi ni umi ni ikimasu.
examples.en: I will go to the sea during the summer vacation.
examples.promptEn: State that you are going to the beach during summer vacation using 〜に行きます

title: Noun の あとで (Noun no atode)
short_explanation: Expresses the order of events; 'after', 'later than'.
long_explanation: The の あとで grammar point is used to express the order of events, specifying that an action occurs after or later than the noun mentioned. It translates to 'after' or 'later than' in English. This structure is simply formed by attaching の あとで to the noun.
formation: Noun + の + あとで

examples.jp: 朝ご飯のあとで、歯を磨きます。
examples.romaji: Asagohan no atode, ha wo migakimasu.
examples.en: After breakfast, I brush my teeth.
examples.promptEn: State that after breakfast, you brush your teeth using 〜のあとで

examples.jp: 映画のあとで、レストランで夕食を食べました。
examples.romaji: Eiga no atode, resutoran de yuushoku o tabemashita.
examples.en: After the movie, we ate dinner at a restaurant.
examples.promptEn: State that after the movie, you had dinner at a restaurant using 〜のあとで

examples.jp: 会議のあとで、上司と話し合います。
examples.romaji: Kaigi no atode, joushi to hanashiaimasu.
examples.en: I will discuss with my boss after the meeting.
examples.promptEn: State that you will talk with your boss after the meeting using 〜のあとで

examples.jp: 晩ご飯のあとで、散歩に行きました。
examples.romaji: Bangohan no atode, sanpo ni ikimashita.
examples.en: After dinner, I went for a walk.
examples.promptEn: State that after dinner, you went for a walk using 〜のあとで

title: Noun の 前に (Noun no mae ni)
short_explanation: Used to describe a location or position 'in front of' a noun.
long_explanation: The grammar point Noun の 前に is used to describe a location or position 'in front of' a noun. It is formed by adding の 前に after the noun it refers to. (Note that 'Noun の 前に' can also mean 'before [Noun]' in time contexts, but these examples focus on physical location.)
formation: Noun + の + 前に

examples.jp: 駅の前にコンビニがあります。
examples.romaji: Eki no mae ni konbini ga arimasu.
examples.en: There is a convenience store in front of the station.
examples.promptEn: State that there is a convenience store in front of the station using 〜の前に

examples.jp: 家の前に車を止めてください。
examples.romaji: Ie no mae ni kuruma wo tomete kudasai.
examples.en: Please park the car in front of the house.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to park your car in front of the house using 〜の前に

examples.jp: 私の前に彼が立っていました。
examples.romaji: Watashi no mae ni kare ga tatte imashita.
examples.en: He was standing in front of me.
examples.promptEn: State that he was standing in front of you using 〜の前に

examples.jp: ホテルの前にタクシーが来た。
examples.romaji: Hoteru no mae ni takushii ga kita.
examples.en: A taxi came in front of the hotel.
examples.promptEn: State that a taxi pulled up in front of the hotel using 〜の前に

title: Noun は～ (Noun wa〜)
short_explanation: Used to mark the topic of a sentence; 'as for', 'speaking of'.
long_explanation: The は (wa) particle is used to indicate the topic of a sentence. It is usually translated as 'as for', 'speaking of', or it simply marks what the sentence is about. This is different from が (ga), which marks the subject of a verb.
formation: Noun + は

examples.jp: 私は日本の料理が好きです。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa Nihon no ryouri ga suki desu.
examples.en: As for me, I like Japanese cuisine.
examples.promptEn: State that you like Japanese food using 〜は

examples.jp: 彼は英語が上手です。
examples.romaji: Kare wa eigo ga jouzu desu.
examples.en: As for him, he is good at English.
examples.promptEn: State that he is good at English using 〜は

examples.jp: この本は面白いです。
examples.romaji: Kono hon wa omoshiroi desu.
examples.en: As for this book, it's interesting.
examples.promptEn: State that this book is interesting using 〜は

examples.jp: 今日は暑いですね。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa atsui desu ne.
examples.en: Speaking of today, it's hot, isn't it?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether it's hot today, isn't it using 〜は

title: Noun も〜 (Noun mo~)
short_explanation: Indicates that the action or state is the same for multiple items or people; 'also', 'as well'.
long_explanation: The も grammar point is used after a noun to indicate that the action or state is the same for multiple items or people. It means 'also', 'as well', or 'too' in English. も often replaces は or が in the sentence to show that the same statement applies to this additional noun.
formation: Noun + も

examples.jp: 私も日本語を勉強しています。
examples.romaji: Watashi mo nihongo wo benkyou shiteimasu.
examples.en: I am also studying Japanese.
examples.promptEn: State that you are studying Japanese, too using 〜も〜

examples.jp: 彼もケーキが好きです。
examples.romaji: Kare mo keeki ga suki desu.
examples.en: He also likes cake.
examples.promptEn: State that he likes cake, too using 〜も〜

examples.jp: 東京も大阪も観光スポットがたくさんあります。
examples.romaji: Toukyou mo Oosaka mo kankou supotto ga takusan arimasu.
examples.en: There are many tourist spots in both Tokyo and Osaka.
examples.promptEn: State that both Tokyo and Osaka have many tourist attractions using 〜も〜

examples.jp: この映画もあの映画も面白かった。
examples.romaji: Kono eiga mo ano eiga mo omoshirokatta.
examples.en: Both this movie and that movie were interesting.
examples.promptEn: State that both this movie and that movie were interesting using 〜も〜

title: Noun や Noun など～ (Noun ya Noun nado)
short_explanation: Lists items or examples but not exhaustively; 'such as', 'like', 'and so on'.
long_explanation: The や...など grammar point is used to list a few items or examples that belong to a similar category or context, but it is not exhaustive. It can be translated as 'such as', 'like', or 'and so on' in English. This grammar pattern is used with nouns.
formation: Noun1 + や + Noun2 + など

examples.jp: 彼は野菜や果物などを食べるのが好きです。
examples.romaji: Kare wa yasai ya kudamono nado o taberu no ga suki desu.
examples.en: He likes to eat things like vegetables and fruits.
examples.promptEn: State that he likes to eat vegetables, fruits, and other foods using contrast 〜やNounなど

examples.jp: 日本の都市や東京、大阪などに行きたいです。
examples.romaji: Nihon no toshi ya Toukyou, Oosaka nado ni ikitai desu.
examples.en: I want to go to Japanese cities such as Tokyo, Osaka, and so on.
examples.promptEn: State that you want to visit cities in Japan, such as Tokyo and Osaka using contrast 〜やNounなど

examples.jp: 彼女は猫や犬など動物が好きです。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa neko ya inu nado doubutsu ga suki desu.
examples.en: She likes animals like cats, dogs, and so on.
examples.promptEn: State that she likes animals such as cats and dogs using contrast 〜やNounなど

examples.jp: この本屋では漫画や小説などたくさんの本が売られています。
examples.romaji: Kono honya de wa manga ya shousetsu nado takusan no hon ga urarete imasu.
examples.en: In this bookstore, many books such as manga and novels are sold.
examples.promptEn: State that this bookstore sells a wide variety of books, including manga and novels using contrast 〜やNounなど

title: Noun を〜 (Noun wo〜)
short_explanation: Indicates the direct object of a verb.
long_explanation: The を (wo) particle is used to mark the direct object of a verb in a sentence. It shows the noun that the action (verb) is performed on. The particle を is usually pronounced as 'o' in spoken Japanese.
formation: Noun + を + Verb

examples.jp: 私は本を読みます。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa hon wo yomimasu.
examples.en: I read a book.
examples.promptEn: State that you read books using 〜を〜

examples.jp: 彼はケーキを食べました。
examples.romaji: Kare wa keeki wo tabemashita.
examples.en: He ate a cake.
examples.promptEn: State that he ate the cake using 〜を〜

examples.jp: 母はコーヒーを飲むのが好きです。
examples.romaji: Haha wa koohii wo nomu no ga suki desu.
examples.en: My mother likes to drink coffee.
examples.promptEn: State that my mother likes to drink coffee using 〜を〜

examples.jp: 友達が私のペンを使いました。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ga watashi no pen wo tsukaimashita.
examples.en: My friend used my pen.
examples.promptEn: State that my friend used your pen using 〜を〜

title: Verb た あとで (ta ato de)
short_explanation: Indicates an action that takes place after another action.
long_explanation: The たあとで grammar point is used to indicate that one action takes place after another action is completed. It means 'after' or 'after doing' in English. The formation is created with the た form (past tense) of a verb, followed by あとで (ato de).
formation: Verb-た form + あとで

examples.jp: 宿題をしたあとで、テレビを見ました。
examples.romaji: Shukudai wo shita ato de, terebi wo mimashita.
examples.en: After doing my homework, I watched TV.
examples.promptEn: State that after you finished your homework, you watched TV using 〜たあとで

examples.jp: 朝ごはんを食べたあとで、歯を磨きます。
examples.romaji: Asagohan wo tabeta ato de, ha wo migakimasu.
examples.en: After eating breakfast, I brush my teeth.
examples.promptEn: State that after eating breakfast, you brush your teeth using 〜たあとで

examples.jp: 仕事が終わったあとで、ジムに行く予定です。
examples.romaji: Shigoto ga owatta ato de, jimu ni iku yotei desu.
examples.en: After finishing work, I plan to go to the gym.
examples.promptEn: State that you plan to go to the gym after work using 〜たあとで

examples.jp: 映画を見たあとで、カフェでコーヒーを飲みました。
examples.romaji: Eiga wo mita ato de, kafe de koohii wo nomimashita.
examples.en: After watching the movie, I drank coffee at a cafe.
examples.promptEn: State that after watching the movie, you had coffee at a café using 〜たあとで

title: Verb たいです (taidesu)
short_explanation: Express desire or want to do something; 'I want to', 'I would like to'.
long_explanation: The たいです grammar point is used to express the speaker's desire or want to perform a certain action. It can be translated as 'I want to' or 'I would like to' in English. The formation differs depending on whether the verb is a る-verb or an う-verb.
formation: る-Verb: Remove る and add たいです, う-Verb: Replace the final verb character with the ～い form and add たいです, Exception: する becomes したいです

examples.jp: 私は寿司を食べたいです。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa sushi wo tabetai desu.
examples.en: I want to eat sushi.
examples.promptEn: State that you want to eat sushi using desire 〜たいです

examples.jp: 彼は日本に行きたいです。
examples.romaji: Kare wa Nihon ni ikitai desu.
examples.en: He wants to go to Japan.
examples.promptEn: State that he wants to go to Japan using desire 〜たいです

examples.jp: 彼女は英語を勉強したいです。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa eigo wo benkyou shitai desu.
examples.en: She wants to study English.
examples.promptEn: State that she wants to study English using desire 〜たいです

examples.jp: 子供たちは遊びたいです。
examples.romaji: Kodomo-tachi wa asobitai desu.
examples.en: The children want to play.
examples.promptEn: State that the children want to play using desire 〜たいです

title: Verb て～ (Verb + te～)
short_explanation: A verb conjugation that connects actions or states.
long_explanation: The ～て form of a verb is used to connect actions or states in a sequence, implying that the first action is completed before the second one starts. The ～て form is frequently used in casual speech, and it can also be used in polite speech when combined with certain auxiliary verbs like ください (kudasai) or いる (iru).
formation: Verb (Group 1) - Replace last syllable with 〜て, Verb (Group 2) - Replace 'る' with 〜て, Verb (Group 3) - する becomes して, くる becomes きて

examples.jp: コーヒーを飲んで、出かけます。
examples.romaji: Koohii o nonde, dekakemasu.
examples.en: After drinking coffee, I will go out.
examples.promptEn: State that you will have some coffee and then head out using 〜て

examples.jp: 買い物をして、家に帰りましょう。
examples.romaji: Kaimono o shite, ie ni kaerimashou.
examples.en: Let's go shopping and then go home.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you go shopping and then head home using 〜て

examples.jp: 宿題をして、寝ます。
examples.romaji: Shukudai o shite, nemasu.
examples.en: After doing my homework, I will sleep.
examples.promptEn: State that you will do your homework and then go to bed using 〜て

examples.jp: 友達を待って、一緒に映画を見に行きます。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi o matte, issho ni eiga o mini ikimasu.
examples.en: I will wait for my friend and go watch a movie together.
examples.promptEn: State that you are waiting for your friend so you can go see a movie together using 〜て

title: Verb て います (Verb te imasu)
short_explanation: Express ongoing action or state; 'is doing', 'is doing (continuous)', 'has been doing'.
long_explanation: The て います grammar point is used to express an action that is ongoing, continuous, or has been happening. It is formed by conjugating the verb in its て-form and adding います. It can be translated as 'is doing', 'is doing (continuous)', or 'has been doing' in English.
formation: Verb て-form + います

examples.jp: 彼女は今ピアノを弾いています。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa ima piano wo hiite imasu.
examples.en: She is playing the piano now.
examples.promptEn: State that she is playing the piano right now using 〜ています

examples.jp: 私たちは日本語を勉強しています。
examples.romaji: Watashitachi wa nihongo wo benkyou shiteimasu.
examples.en: We are studying Japanese.
examples.promptEn: State that we are studying Japanese using 〜ています

examples.jp: 彼は映画を見ています。
examples.romaji: Kare wa eiga wo miteimasu.
examples.en: He is watching a movie.
examples.promptEn: State that he is watching a movie using 〜ています

examples.jp: 入っていますので、お待ちください。
examples.romaji: Haitteimasu node, omachi kudasai.
examples.en: I am in, so please wait.
examples.promptEn: State that it's loading, so please wait using 〜ています

title: Verb てから～ (〜te kara)
short_explanation: Express a sequence of actions or events; 'after', 'since', 'once'.
long_explanation: The ～てから grammar point is used to indicate the sequence of actions or events, meaning that one action or event occurs after another. It can be translated as 'after', 'since', or 'once' in English. The て-form indicates the first action and から shows the sequence.
formation: Verb-て形 + から

examples.jp: 宿題をしてから、テレビを見ました。
examples.romaji: Shukudai wo shite kara, terebi wo mimashita.
examples.en: I watched TV after doing my homework.
examples.promptEn: State that you did your homework and then watched TV using reason 〜てから

examples.jp: 食べてから、歯を磨きましょう。
examples.romaji: Tabete kara, ha wo migakimashou.
examples.en: Let's brush our teeth after eating.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you brush your teeth after eating using reason 〜てから

examples.jp: 仕事が終わってから、友達と飲みに行きます。
examples.romaji: Shigoto ga owatte kara, tomodachi to nomi ni ikimasu.
examples.en: I will go drinking with my friends after work is done.
examples.promptEn: State that after work, you are going out for drinks with your friends using reason 〜てから

examples.jp: 学校が終わってから、図書館で勉強します。
examples.romaji: Gakkou ga owatte kara, toshokan de benkyou shimasu.
examples.en: I will study in the library after school is over.
examples.promptEn: State that after school, you study at the library using reason 〜てから

title: Verb て ください (Verb-te kudasai)
short_explanation: A request or command; 'please do'.
long_explanation: The て ください grammar point is used to make a request or command someone to do something politely. The verb is conjugated into its て-form and followed by ください, which means 'please'. This structure is used when asking someone to do something with a polite and respectful tone.
formation: Verb-て form + ください

examples.jp: ドアを開けてください。
examples.romaji: Doa wo akete kudasai.
examples.en: Please open the door.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to open the door using polite request 〜てください

examples.jp: 電話番号を教えてください。
examples.romaji: Denwa bangou wo oshiete kudasai.
examples.en: Please tell me your phone number.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to tell you your phone number using polite request 〜てください

examples.jp: ゆっくり話してください。
examples.romaji: Yukkuri hanashite kudasai.
examples.en: Please speak slowly.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to speak slowly using polite request 〜てください

examples.jp: コーヒーを一つ持ってきてください。
examples.romaji: Koohii wo hitotsu motte kite kudasai.
examples.en: Please bring me a coffee.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to bring you a cup of coffee using polite request 〜てください

title: Verb ないで ください (〜naide kudasai)
short_explanation: Used to make a polite request for someone not to do something; 'please don't'.
long_explanation: The grammar point Verb ないで ください is used to make a polite request for someone not to do a certain action. In English, it can be translated as 'please don't'. To form this expression, take the verb in its negative form (ない-form) and add で ください.
formation: Verb-ない-form + で ください

examples.jp: タバコを吸わないでください。
examples.romaji: Tabako wo suwanaide kudasai.
examples.en: Please don't smoke.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to do not smoke using polite request 〜ないでください

examples.jp: ここで走らないでください。
examples.romaji: Koko de hashiranaide kudasai.
examples.en: Please don't run here.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to do not run here using polite request 〜ないでください

examples.jp: 大きな声で話さないでください。
examples.romaji: Ookina koe de hanasanaide kudasai.
examples.en: Please don't speak loudly.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to do not speak loudly using polite request 〜ないでください

examples.jp: 写真を撮らないでください。
examples.romaji: Shashin wo toranaide kudasai.
examples.en: Please don't take photos.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to do not take photos using polite request 〜ないでください

title: Noun に 戻ります (Noun ni modorimasu)
short_explanation: Expresses the action of returning to a previous state, place, or condition.
long_explanation: The Noun に 戻ります grammar point is used to express going back or reverting to a previous state, place, or condition. 戻る (modoru) literally means 'to go back' or 'to revert'. This is often used after a change has occurred, indicating that something is being undone or returned to its original form.
formation: Noun + に + 戻ります

examples.jp: 冷蔵庫に入れると、溶けたアイスクリームは固体に戻ります。
examples.romaji: Reizouko ni ireru to, toketa aisukuriimu wa kotai ni modorimasu.
examples.en: When put in the refrigerator, the melted ice cream returns to its solid state.
examples.promptEn: Ask whether when placed in the refrigerator, melted ice cream turns back into a solid using conditional 〜に戻ります

examples.jp: 休暇が終わったら、仕事に戻ります。
examples.romaji: Kyuuka ga owattara, shigoto ni modorimasu.
examples.en: When the vacation ends, I will return to work.
examples.promptEn: State that once your vacation is over, you will go back to work using conditional 〜に戻ります

examples.jp: リモートワークが終わった後、元のオフィスに戻ります。
examples.romaji: Rimooto waaku ga owatta ato, moto no ofisu ni modorimasu.
examples.en: After remote work is over, we will return to our original office.
examples.promptEn: State that after your remote work is over, you will return to your original office using conditional 〜に戻ります

examples.jp: 外国で勉強した後、日本に帰ります。
examples.romaji: Gaikoku de benkyou shita ato, Nihon ni kaerimasu.
examples.en: After studying abroad, I will return to Japan.
examples.promptEn: State that after studying abroad, you will return to Japan using conditional 〜に戻ります

title: Verb に 来ます (Verb ni kimasu)
short_explanation: Expresses the purpose of coming to a place; 'come to (do something)'.
long_explanation: The grammar point Verb に きます is used to express the purpose of coming to a place to perform an action. It can be translated as 'come to (do something)' in English. To form this expression, use the verb's ます-stem (i.e., remove ます) followed by に きます.
formation: Verb (ます-stem) + に + 来ます

examples.jp: 友達に会いに来ました。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ni ai ni kimashita.
examples.en: I came to meet my friend.
examples.promptEn: State that you came to see your friend using purpose 〜に来ます

examples.jp: 映画を見に来ました。
examples.romaji: Eiga wo mi ni kimashita.
examples.en: I came to watch a movie.
examples.promptEn: State that you came to see a movie using purpose 〜に来ます

examples.jp: 先生に質問しに来ました。
examples.romaji: Sensei ni shitsumon shi ni kimashita.
examples.en: I came to ask the teacher a question.
examples.promptEn: State that you came to ask the teacher a question using purpose 〜に来ます

examples.jp: 買い物をしに来ました。
examples.romaji: Kaimono wo shi ni kimashita.
examples.en: I came to go shopping.
examples.promptEn: State that you came here to go shopping using purpose 〜に来ます

title: Verb に 行きます (Verb ni ikimasu)
short_explanation: To go (somewhere) in order to do an action.
long_explanation: The grammar point Verb に 行きます is used when expressing that someone is going to a certain place with the purpose of doing a specific action. Form it by taking the verb's ます-stem (for suru-verbs, remove する and add し) and then adding に 行きます.
formation: Verb (ます-stem) + に + 行きます

examples.jp: 公園に遊びに行きます。
examples.romaji: Kouen ni asobi ni ikimasu.
examples.en: I will go to the park to play.
examples.promptEn: State that you are going to the park to play using purpose 〜に行きます

examples.jp: 図書館に勉強しに行きます。
examples.romaji: Toshokan ni benkyou shi ni ikimasu.
examples.en: I will go to the library to study.
examples.promptEn: State that you are going to the library to study using purpose 〜に行きます

examples.jp: スーパーに買い物に行きます。
examples.romaji: Suupaa ni kaimono ni ikimasu.
examples.en: I will go to the supermarket to do some shopping.
examples.promptEn: State that you are going to the supermarket to shop using purpose 〜に行きます

examples.jp: 映画館に映画を見に行きます。
examples.romaji: Eigakan ni eiga wo mi ni ikimasu.
examples.en: I will go to the movie theater to watch a movie.
examples.promptEn: State that you are going to the movie theater to watch a movie using purpose 〜に行きます

title: Verb ましょう (mashou)
short_explanation: Making a suggestion or invitation; 'let's' or 'shall we'.
long_explanation: The ましょう grammar point is used to suggest or invite someone to do something in a polite and friendly way. It can be translated as 'let's' or 'shall we' in English. This grammar point is formed by attaching ましょう to the stem of the verb (i.e. remove ます).
formation: Verb (ます-stem) + ましょう

examples.jp: 一緒に映画を見ましょう。
examples.romaji: Issho ni eiga wo mimashou.
examples.en: Let's watch a movie together.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you watch a movie together using suggestion 〜ましょう

examples.jp: 散歩しましょう。
examples.romaji: Sanpo shimashou.
examples.en: Let's take a walk.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you go for a walk using suggestion 〜ましょう

examples.jp: 今晩、食事に行きましょう。
examples.romaji: Konban, shokuji ni ikimashou.
examples.en: Let's go out for dinner tonight.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you go out for dinner tonight using suggestion 〜ましょう

examples.jp: 明日勉強しましょう。
examples.romaji: Ashita benkyou shimashou.
examples.en: Let's study tomorrow.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you study tomorrow using suggestion 〜ましょう

title: Verb ましょうか。 (〜mashou ka.)
short_explanation: Used to make a polite suggestion or offer help; 'shall we', 'should we', 'do you want me to'.
long_explanation: The ましょうか grammar point is used to make a polite suggestion, propose an action, or offer help. It can be translated as 'shall we', 'should we', or 'do you want me to' in English. This formation is used with verbs in their ます-form, replacing ます with ましょう and adding か.
formation: Verb (ます-stem) + ましょうか

examples.jp: 一緒に映画を見に行きましょうか。
examples.romaji: Issho ni eiga wo mi ni ikimashou ka.
examples.en: Shall we go see a movie together?
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you shall you go see a movie together? using suggestion 〜ましょうか

examples.jp: コーヒーをもう一杯飲みましょうか。
examples.romaji: Koohii wo mou ippai nomimashou ka.
examples.en: Should we have another cup of coffee?
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you shall you have another cup of coffee? using suggestion 〜ましょうか

examples.jp: あなたの荷物を持ちましょうか。
examples.romaji: Anata no nimotsu wo mochimashou ka.
examples.en: Do you want me to carry your luggage?
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you would you like you to carry your luggage? using suggestion 〜ましょうか

examples.jp: 窓を開けましょうか。
examples.romaji: Mado wo akemashou ka.
examples.en: Shall I open the window?
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you shall you open the window? using suggestion 〜ましょうか

title: Verb ませんか。 (Verb-masenka)
short_explanation: An invitation or suggestion; 'won't you', 'why don't you', 'shall we'.
long_explanation: The ませんか grammar point is used for making invitations or suggestions in a polite manner. The verb is conjugated to its ます form and replaced with ませんか. This can be translated as 'won't you', 'why don't you', or 'shall we' in English.
formation: Verb (ます-form) + ませんか

examples.jp: 一緒に映画を見ませんか。
examples.romaji: Issho ni eiga wo mimasenka.
examples.en: Won't you watch a movie together with me?
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you would you like to watch a movie with you? using suggestion 〜ませんか

examples.jp: 明日のパーティーに参加しませんか。
examples.romaji: Ashita no paatii ni sanka shimasenka.
examples.en: Why don't you join tomorrow's party?
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you would you like to come to the party tomorrow? using suggestion 〜ませんか

examples.jp: 週末にピクニックに行きませんか。
examples.romaji: Shuumatsu ni pikunikku ni ikimasenka.
examples.en: Shall we go for a picnic on the weekend?
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you how about going on a picnic this weekend? using suggestion 〜ませんか

examples.jp: 一緒に勉強しませんか。
examples.romaji: Issho ni benkyou shimasenka.
examples.en: How about studying together?
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you why don't you study together? using suggestion 〜ませんか

title: Verb ること～ (〜ru koto)
short_explanation: Express an action or event as a noun; 'the act of', 'doing'.
long_explanation: The ること grammar point is used to nominalize or turn a verb into a noun, which represents the action or event itself as a concept. It can be translated as 'the act of' or simply 'doing' in English. This formation is used with verbs in the dictionary (ru-)form.
formation: Verb (dictionary form) + こと

examples.jp: 泳ぐことが大好きです。
examples.romaji: Oyogu koto ga daisuki desu.
examples.en: I love swimming.
examples.promptEn: State that you love swimming using 〜ること

examples.jp: 日本語を勉強することは楽しいです。
examples.romaji: Nihongo wo benkyou suru koto wa tanoshii desu.
examples.en: Studying Japanese is fun.
examples.promptEn: State that studying Japanese is fun using 〜ること

examples.jp: 友達と話すことがストレスを軽減します。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi to hanasu koto ga sutoresu wo keigen shimasu.
examples.en: Talking with friends reduces stress.
examples.promptEn: State that talking with friends helps reduce stress using 〜ること

examples.jp: 彼は歌うことが得意です。
examples.romaji: Kare wa utau koto ga tokui desu.
examples.en: He is good at singing.
examples.promptEn: State that he is good at singing using 〜ること

title: Verb る こと が できます (ru koto ga dekimasu)
short_explanation: Express the potential form, or the ability to do something.
long_explanation: The 〜ることができます grammar point is used to express that someone is capable of doing something or that something is possible. It is essentially the potential form of the verb. The formation is made by changing the verb to a noun phrase with こと and then adding ができます.
formation: Verb (dictionary form) + ことができます

examples.jp: この問題を解くことができます。
examples.romaji: Kono mondai o toku koto ga dekimasu.
examples.en: I can solve this problem.
examples.promptEn: State that you can solve this problem using potential 〜ることができます

examples.jp: 彼は英語を話すことができます。
examples.romaji: Kare wa eigo o hanasu koto ga dekimasu.
examples.en: He can speak English.
examples.promptEn: State that he can speak English using potential 〜ることができます

examples.jp: 私は高い所に登ることができません。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa takai tokoro ni noboru koto ga dekimasen.
examples.en: I can't climb to high places.
examples.promptEn: State that you can't climb to high places using potential 〜ることができます

examples.jp: 彼女はピアノを弾くことができます。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa piano o hiku koto ga dekimasu.
examples.en: She can play the piano.
examples.promptEn: State that she can play the piano using potential 〜ることができます

title: Verb る こと ができる (ru koto ga dekiru)
short_explanation: Expresses the potential form; 'can', 'be able to', 'is possible'.
long_explanation: The る こと ができる grammar point is used to express the potential form of a verb, meaning the ability or possibility to do something. It can be translated as 'can', 'be able to', or 'is possible' in English. This grammar is often used with verbs ending in る, but can also apply to other verbs once they are in the dictionary form.
formation: Verb (dictionary form) + ことができる

examples.jp: この問題を解くことができる？
examples.romaji: Kono mondai o toku koto ga dekiru?
examples.en: Can you solve this problem?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether can you solve this problem using potential 〜ることができる

examples.jp: 彼は泳ぐことができます。
examples.romaji: Kare wa oyogu koto ga dekimasu.
examples.en: He can swim.
examples.promptEn: State that he can swim using potential 〜ることができる

examples.jp: 日本に行くことができて、とても嬉しいです。
examples.romaji: Nihon ni iku koto ga dekite, totemo ureshii desu.
examples.en: I'm very happy that I can go to Japan.
examples.promptEn: State that you are so happy to be able to go to Japan using potential 〜ることができる

examples.jp: 彼女はピアノを弾くことができます。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa piano o hiku koto ga dekimasu.
examples.en: She can play the piano.
examples.promptEn: State that she can play the piano using potential 〜ることができる

title: Verb る の～ (Verb + ru + no~)
short_explanation: Used to express the purpose or reason in casual speech, or nominalize the verb with の.
long_explanation: The る の～ grammar point is a casual spoken pattern that can nominalize a verb or explain a purpose/reason by adding の. It's often seen in everyday conversation, and can be used for nuance such as giving an explanation. It's similar to ること, but is more colloquial or explanatory in tone.
formation: Verb (dictionary form) + の (casual)

examples.jp: 買い物をするために、銀行でお金をおろすの。
examples.romaji: Kaimono o suru tame ni, ginkou de okane o orosu no.
examples.en: I'm withdrawing money at the bank so I can go shopping.
examples.promptEn: State that you are going to the bank to withdraw money so you can go shopping using reason 〜るの

examples.jp: 友達にプレゼントをあげるので、ケーキを焼くの。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ni purezento o ageru node, keeki o yaku no.
examples.en: I'm baking a cake because I'm giving my friend a present.
examples.promptEn: State that you are baking a cake because you are giving it to a friend as a present using reason 〜るの

examples.jp: ダイエットを始めるので、ジムに入会するの。
examples.romaji: Daietto o hajimeru node, jimu ni nyuukai suru no.
examples.en: I’m joining a gym since I'm starting a diet.
examples.promptEn: State that you are starting a diet, so you are joining a gym using reason 〜るの

examples.jp: 軽い食事がいいので、サラダを作るの。
examples.romaji: Karui shokuji ga ii node, sarada o tsukuru no.
examples.en: I'm making a salad because I want a light meal.
examples.promptEn: State that you want something light to eat, so you are making a salad using reason 〜るの

title: Verb る 前に (ru mae ni)
short_explanation: Used to express 'before' in a sense of an action must be done before another action or event.
long_explanation: The る前に (ru mae ni) grammar point is used to indicate that an action (in the dictionary form) should be completed before another action occurs or before a specific event happens.
formation: Verb (dictionary form) + 前に

examples.jp: 出かける前に、部屋を掃除してください。
examples.romaji: Dekakeru mae ni, heya o souji shite kudasai.
examples.en: Please clean the room before leaving.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to clean your room before you go out using 〜る前に

examples.jp: 寝る前に、歯を磨きます。
examples.romaji: Neru mae ni, ha o migakimasu.
examples.en: I brush my teeth before going to bed.
examples.promptEn: State that you brush your teeth before going to bed using 〜る前に

examples.jp: 雨が降る前に、洗濯物を取り込むこと。
examples.romaji: Ame ga furu mae ni, sentakumono o torikomu koto.
examples.en: Take in the laundry before it rains.
examples.promptEn: State that bring the laundry in before it rains using 〜る前に

examples.jp: 会議が始まる前に、資料を準備しましょう。
examples.romaji: Kaigi ga hajimaru mae ni, shiryou o junbi shimashou.
examples.en: Let's prepare the documents before the meeting starts.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you prepare the materials before the meeting begins using 〜る前に

title: あまり～ありません (amari ~ arimasen)
short_explanation: Express 'not very', 'not much', or 'not really' when describing a negative state or situation.
long_explanation: The grammar point あまり～ありません is used to describe a negative state or condition and indicate that it's not very, not much, or not really. It is commonly used with verbs in the negative form and can be used with い-adjectives, な-adjectives, and nouns.
formation: あまり + Verb-ないform + ありません / あまり + い-Adjective-く ありません / あまり + な-Adjective・Noun じゃありません

examples.jp: 彼はあまり疲れていません。
examples.romaji: Kare wa amari tsukareteimasen.
examples.en: He is not really tired.
examples.promptEn: State that he isn't very tired using 〜あまり～ありません

examples.jp: 彼女はあまり早くないですよ。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa amari hayakunai desu yo.
examples.en: She is not very fast.
examples.promptEn: State that she isn't that fast using 〜あまり～ありません

examples.jp: 私はあまり勉強しないです。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa amari benkyou shinai desu.
examples.en: I don't study very much.
examples.promptEn: State that you don't study much using 〜あまり～ありません

examples.jp: あまりお金がありません。
examples.romaji: Amari okane ga arimasen.
examples.en: I don't have much money.
examples.promptEn: State that you don't have much money using 〜あまり～ありません

title: あまり～ないです (amari ~ nai desu)
