short_explanation: Express 'not really' or 'not very'; used to soften a negative statement.
long_explanation: The あまり～ないです grammar point is used to express that something is 'not really' or 'not very' to a certain extent. It is often used to soften a negative statement. It can be used with verbs, い-adjectives, and な-adjectives in their negative forms.
formation: あまり + Verb-ないform + です / あまり + い-Adjective-くない + です / あまり + な-Adjective-じゃない + です

examples.jp: あまり食べないです。
examples.romaji: Amari tabenai desu.
examples.en: I don't really eat much.
examples.promptEn: State that you don't eat much using 〜あまり～ないです

examples.jp: この映画はあまり面白くないです。
examples.romaji: Kono eiga wa amari omoshirokunai desu.
examples.en: This movie is not really interesting.
examples.promptEn: State that this movie isn't very interesting using 〜あまり～ないです

examples.jp: 彼はあまり親切じゃないです。
examples.romaji: Kare wa amari shinsetsu ja nai desu.
examples.en: He is not very kind.
examples.promptEn: State that he isn't very kind using 〜あまり～ないです

examples.jp: 私はあまり日本語が上手じゃないです。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa amari nihongo ga jouzu ja nai desu.
examples.en: I am not very good at Japanese.
examples.promptEn: State that you are not very good at Japanese using 〜あまり～ないです

title: ～あります (〜arimasu)
short_explanation: Indicate possession or existence of inanimate objects; 'there is', 'there are'.
long_explanation: The あります grammar point is used to indicate the possession or existence of inanimate objects. It can be translated as 'there is' or 'there are' in English. It is different from います, which is used for people and most living creatures. あります is commonly used with particle が to mark the object.
formation: Object + が + あります

examples.jp: 教室に机があります。
examples.romaji: Kyoushitsu ni tsukue ga arimasu.
examples.en: There is a desk in the classroom.
examples.promptEn: State that there are desks in the classroom using 〜あります

examples.jp: この公園にたくさんの花があります。
examples.romaji: Kono kouen ni takusan no hana ga arimasu.
examples.en: There are many flowers in this park.
examples.promptEn: State that there are many flowers in this park using 〜あります

examples.jp: 駅の近くにコンビニがあります。
examples.romaji: Eki no chikaku ni konbini ga arimasu.
examples.en: There is a convenience store near the station.
examples.promptEn: State that there is a convenience store near the station using 〜あります

examples.jp: 家の中に古いテレビがあります。
examples.romaji: Ie no naka ni furui terebi ga arimasu.
examples.en: There is an old TV inside the house.
examples.promptEn: State that there is an old TV in the house using 〜あります

title: ～いかがですか。 (〜ikaga desu ka.)
short_explanation: A polite way to ask someone's thoughts, opinions, or preferences; 'how about', 'how is'.
long_explanation: The ～いかがですか grammar point is used to politely ask someone's thoughts, opinions, or preferences. It can be translated as 'how about' or 'how is' in English. The formation is quite straightforward when used with verbs or nouns.
formation: Noun + は + いかがですか / (Verb-て form + は) いかがですか

examples.jp: お茶はいかがですか？
examples.romaji: Ocha wa ikaga desu ka?
examples.en: How about some tea?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether would you like some tea using 〜いかがですか

examples.jp: このドレスはいかがですか？
examples.romaji: Kono doresu wa ikaga desu ka?
examples.en: How about this dress?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether how about this dress using 〜いかがですか

examples.jp: ケーキを食べてはいかがですか？
examples.romaji: Keeki wo tabete wa ikaga desu ka?
examples.en: How about eating some cake?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether why don't you try some cake using 〜いかがですか

examples.jp: 映画を見てはいかがですか？
examples.romaji: Eiga wo mite wa ikaga desu ka?
examples.en: How about watching a movie?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether how about watching a movie using 〜いかがですか

title: いくつ～ (ikutsu~)
short_explanation: Used to express 'how many' or ask for the number of something.
long_explanation: The grammar point いくつ is used when asking or expressing 'how many' of something there are, or to indicate an unspecified number. In English, it can be translated as 'how many' or 'several'.
formation: いくつ + Noun (optional)

examples.jp: リンゴはいくつありますか？
examples.romaji: Ringo wa ikutsu arimasu ka?
examples.en: How many apples are there?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether how many apples are there using 〜いくつ

examples.jp: いくつかの問題を解決しなければなりません。
examples.romaji: Ikutsu ka no mondai o kaiketsu shinakereba narimasen.
examples.en: I have to solve several problems.
examples.promptEn: State that there are several problems that need to be solved using 〜いくつ

examples.jp: あなたはいくつの言語を話せますか？
examples.romaji: Anata wa ikutsu no gengo o hanasemasu ka?
examples.en: How many languages can you speak?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether how many languages do you speak using 〜いくつ

examples.jp: パーティーにはいくつかの飲み物があります。
examples.romaji: Paatii ni wa ikutsu ka no nomimono ga arimasu.
examples.en: There are several drinks at the party.
examples.promptEn: State that there are several drinks at the party using 〜いくつ

title: いつか～ (itsuka～)
short_explanation: Indicates an unspecified point in time; 'someday', 'one day', 'at some point'.
long_explanation: The grammar point いつか is used to indicate an unspecified point in time, meaning 'someday', 'one day', or 'at some point' in the future or the past. It can be used in sentences to express hopes, dreams, or possibilities.
formation: いつか + sentence

examples.jp: いつか日本に行きたいです。
examples.romaji: Itsuka Nihon ni ikitai desu.
examples.en: I want to go to Japan someday.
examples.promptEn: State that you want to visit Japan someday using 〜いつか

examples.jp: 彼はいつか有名な作家になるでしょう。
examples.romaji: Kare wa itsuka yuumei na sakka ni naru deshou.
examples.en: He will become a famous writer someday.
examples.promptEn: State that he will become a famous writer someday using 〜いつか

examples.jp: いつかあの山を登りたいと思っています。
examples.romaji: Itsuka ano yama wo noboritai to omotte imasu.
examples.en: I think I want to climb that mountain someday.
examples.promptEn: State that you hope to climb that mountain someday using 〜いつか

examples.jp: 彼女はいつか夢を叶えることができると信じています。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa itsuka yume wo kanaeru koto ga dekiru to shinjiteimasu.
examples.en: I believe she can achieve her dream someday.
examples.promptEn: State that she believes that one day she will be able to make her dream come true using 〜いつか

title: いつでも～ (itsudemo～)
short_explanation: Expresses 'anytime', 'always', or 'whenever'.
long_explanation: The いつでも grammar point is used to express that something occurs, can occur, or is allowed to occur anytime, always, or whenever. It emphasizes the lack of restrictions related to time for a certain action or event.
formation: いつでも + (Verb)

examples.jp: いつでも遊びに来てください。
examples.romaji: Itsudemo asobi ni kite kudasai.
examples.en: Please come to play anytime.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to feel free to come visit anytime using contrast 〜いつでも

examples.jp: 彼女はいつでも笑顔です。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa itsudemo egao desu.
examples.en: She is always smiling.
examples.promptEn: State that she is always smiling using contrast 〜いつでも

examples.jp: いつでも電話で連絡できます。
examples.romaji: Itsudemo denwa de renraku dekimasu.
examples.en: You can contact me by phone anytime.
examples.promptEn: State that you can contact you by phone anytime using contrast 〜いつでも

examples.jp: この店はいつでも混んでいます。
examples.romaji: Kono mise wa itsudemo konde imasu.
examples.en: This store is always crowded.
examples.promptEn: State that this restaurant is always crowded using contrast 〜いつでも

title: いつも～ (itsumo～)
short_explanation: Expressing 'always' or 'usually' in a sentence.
long_explanation: The grammar point いつも (itsumo) is used to express the meaning of 'always' or 'usually' when describing a habitual action or situation. It is often used with the present tense or past tense to show that something is done on a regular basis or has been happening consistently.
formation: いつも + Verb / Adjective / Noun

examples.jp: 彼はいつも遅刻します。
examples.romaji: Kare wa itsumo chikoku shimasu.
examples.en: He is always late.
examples.promptEn: State that he is always late using 〜いつも

examples.jp: 私はいつも優しい犬が好きです。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa itsumo yasashii inu ga suki desu.
examples.en: I always like gentle dogs.
examples.promptEn: State that you always like gentle dogs using 〜いつも

examples.jp: 彼女はいつも静かな場所で勉強します。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa itsumo shizuka na basho de benkyou shimasu.
examples.en: She always studies in a quiet place.
examples.promptEn: State that she always studies in a quiet place using 〜いつも

examples.jp: いつも朝ご飯を食べます。
examples.romaji: Itsumo asagohan wo tabemasu.
examples.en: I always eat breakfast.
examples.promptEn: State that you always eat breakfast using 〜いつも

title: ～て います (～te imasu)
short_explanation: Expresses the present continuous or ongoing action; 'to be doing', 'currently doing'.
long_explanation: The ～て います grammar pattern is used to express that an action is currently happening or ongoing. It can be translated as 'to be doing' or 'currently doing' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is a る-verb, う-verb, or an irregular verb, but all use the verb’s て-form + います.
formation: Verb て-form + います

examples.jp: 今、音楽を聞いています。
examples.romaji: Ima, ongaku wo kiite imasu.
examples.en: I am listening to music right now.
examples.promptEn: State that you are listening to music right now using 〜ています

examples.jp: 父は新聞を読んでいます。
examples.romaji: Chichi wa shinbun wo yonde imasu.
examples.en: My father is reading a newspaper.
examples.promptEn: State that my father is reading the newspaper using 〜ています

examples.jp: 彼女は英語を勉強しています。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa eigo wo benkyou shite imasu.
examples.en: She is studying English.
examples.promptEn: State that she is studying English using 〜ています

examples.jp: 子供たちは公園で遊んでいます。
examples.romaji: Kodomotachi wa kouen de asonde imasu.
examples.en: The children are playing in the park.
examples.promptEn: State that the children are playing in the park using 〜ています

title: ～が (〜ga)
short_explanation: Particle indicating the subject of a sentence or expressing 'but'.
long_explanation: The ～が grammar point is a particle that is used to indicate the subject of a sentence or to express a contrast similar to 'but' in English. It has various functions depending on the context.
formation: Noun + が / い-Adjective + が / な-Adjective + が / Verb + が

examples.jp: 私が学生です。
examples.romaji: Watashi ga gakusei desu.
examples.en: I am a student.
examples.promptEn: State that you are a student using contrast 〜が

examples.jp: このりんごが美味しい。
examples.romaji: Kono ringo ga oishii.
examples.en: This apple is delicious.
examples.promptEn: State that this apple is delicious using contrast 〜が

examples.jp: 彼は頭がいいが、性格が悪い。
examples.romaji: Kare wa atama ga ii ga, seikaku ga warui.
examples.en: He is smart but has a bad personality.
examples.promptEn: State that he's smart, but he has a bad personality using contrast 〜が

examples.jp: 走りたいが、足が痛い。
examples.romaji: Hashiritai ga, ashi ga itai.
examples.en: I want to run, but my leg hurts.
examples.promptEn: State that you want to run, but your leg hurts using contrast 〜が

title: ～が、～ (〜ga, 〜)
short_explanation: Express a contrast between two sentences; 'but', 'however'.
long_explanation: The ～が、～ grammar point is used to express a contrast or contradiction between two sentences or clauses. It can be translated as 'but' or 'however' in English. This grammar point is slightly more formal than けど and is used to show a contrast in the situation.
formation: Sentence 1 + が、+ Sentence 2

examples.jp: デザートは美味しいが、カロリーが高い。
examples.romaji: Dezaato wa oishii ga, karorii ga takai.
examples.en: The dessert is delicious, but it is high in calories.
examples.promptEn: State that dessert is delicious, but it's high in calories using contrast 〜が

examples.jp: 彼は頭がいいが、少し怠け者だ。
examples.romaji: Kare wa atama ga ii ga, sukoshi namakemono da.
examples.en: He is smart, but a bit lazy.
examples.promptEn: State that he is smart, but a bit lazy using contrast 〜が

examples.jp: 会社は利益を上げたが、従業員の給与は上がらなかった。
examples.romaji: Kaisha wa rieki wo ageta ga, juugyouin no kyuuyo wa agaranakatta.
examples.en: The company made a profit, however, the employees' salaries did not increase.
examples.promptEn: State that the company made a profit, but employees' salaries did not increase using contrast 〜が

examples.jp: 外国語を勉強することが楽しいが、時々難しい。
examples.romaji: Gaikokugo wo benkyou suru koto ga tanoshii ga, tokidoki muzukashii.
examples.en: Studying foreign languages is fun, but sometimes difficult.
examples.promptEn: State that studying a foreign language is fun, but sometimes it's difficult using contrast 〜が

title: ～から、～ (〜kara、～)
short_explanation: Expresses reason or cause; 'because', 'since', 'so'.
long_explanation: The ～から grammar point is used to indicate the reason or cause for something. It can be translated as 'because', 'since', or 'so' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
formation: Verb-casual + から / い-Adjective + から / な-Adjective + だから / Noun + だから

examples.jp: 明日は試験があるから、今晩勉強しなければなりません。
examples.romaji: Ashita wa shiken ga aru kara, konban benkyou shinakereba narimasen.
examples.en: Because I have an exam tomorrow, I must study tonight.
examples.promptEn: State that you have a test tomorrow, so you have to study tonight using reason 〜から

examples.jp: この部屋は狭いから、もっと大きい部屋を探しています。
examples.romaji: Kono heya wa semai kara, motto ookii heya wo sagashiteimasu.
examples.en: Since this room is small, I am looking for a bigger one.
examples.promptEn: State that this room is small, so you are looking for a bigger one using reason 〜から

examples.jp: 彼は友達だから、手伝ってくれるでしょう。
examples.romaji: Kare wa tomodachi dakara, tetsudatte kureru deshou.
examples.en: Since he is my friend, he will probably help me.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to since he's your friend, he'll help you, won't he? using reason 〜から

examples.jp: 雨が降ったから、外に出られません。
examples.romaji: Ame ga futta kara, soto ni deraremasen.
examples.en: Because it rained, I can't go outside.
examples.promptEn: State that it rained, so you can't go outside using reason 〜から

title: ～からです (〜kara desu)
short_explanation: Express the reason or cause; 'because', 'since', 'due to'.
long_explanation: The ～からです grammar point is used to state the reason or cause of something, often as a short concluding statement. It can be translated as 'because', 'since', or 'due to' in English. The formation can be used with verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives, or nouns, but be careful with な-adjectives and nouns: typically, it's [Noun/な-adjective] + だからです.
formation: Verb-casual + からです / い-Adjective + からです / な-Adjective + だからです / Noun + だからです

examples.jp: 寒いからです。コートを着ています。
examples.romaji: Samui kara desu. Kooto wo kiteimasu.
examples.en: It’s because it’s cold. That’s why I’m wearing a coat.
examples.promptEn: State that it's cold, so you are wearing a coat using reason 〜からです

examples.jp: この店は安いからです。よく来ます。
examples.romaji: Kono mise wa yasui kara desu. Yoku kimasu.
examples.en: It’s because this store is cheap. That’s why I come often.
examples.promptEn: State that it's because this restaurant is cheap. you come here often using reason 〜からです

examples.jp: 彼は親切だからです。みんなに好かれています。
examples.romaji: Kare wa shinsetsu dakara desu. Minna ni suka-rete imasu.
examples.en: It’s because he’s kind. Everyone likes him.
examples.promptEn: State that it's because he's kind. Everyone likes him using reason 〜からです

examples.jp: 彼女は学生だからです。図書館で勉強しています。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa gakusei dakara desu. Toshokan de benkyou shiteimasu.
examples.en: It’s because she’s a student. She studies at the library.
examples.promptEn: State that it's because she's a student. She's studying at the library using reason 〜からです

title: ～から もらいます (〜kara moraimasu)
short_explanation: To receive something or get someone to do something.
long_explanation: The ～からもらいます grammar point is used to express receiving something from someone or getting someone to do something for you. In English, it can be translated as 'to receive from' or 'to get someone to do something'.
formation: Noun + から + (Verb-て form) + もらいます

examples.jp: 友達からプレゼントをもらいました。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi kara purezento wo moraimashita.
examples.en: I received a present from my friend.
examples.promptEn: State that you received a gift from a friend using reason 〜からもらいます

examples.jp: 先生に宿題を渡してもらいました。
examples.romaji: Sensei ni shukudai wo watashite moraimashita.
examples.en: I had the teacher hand me the homework.
examples.promptEn: State that the teacher gave you your homework using reason 〜からもらいます

examples.jp: お母さんに料理を作ってもらいました。
examples.romaji: Okaasan ni ryouri wo tsukutte moraimashita.
examples.en: I got my mom to cook for me.
examples.promptEn: State that my mom made you a meal using reason 〜からもらいます

examples.jp: 兄に車を貸してもらいました。
examples.romaji: Ani ni kuruma wo kashite moraimashita.
examples.en: I got my older brother to lend me his car.
examples.promptEn: State that my older brother lent you his car using reason 〜からもらいます

title: ～が 私に くれます (〜ga watashi ni kuremasu)
short_explanation: Used to express that someone gives a gift or favor to 'me'; 'someone gives me'.
long_explanation: The ～が私にくれます grammar point is used to express that someone gives 'me' something or does something for me. It can be translated as 'someone gives me' or 'someone does something for me' in English. Typically, the giver is marked by が, and the receiver is 私に (to me).
formation: Person + が + (Thing or Action) + 私に + くれます

examples.jp: 彼がプレゼントを私にくれました。
examples.romaji: Kare ga purezento wo watashi ni kuremashita.
examples.en: He gave me a present.
examples.promptEn: State that he gave you a present using 〜が私にくれます

examples.jp: 友達が宿題を手伝って私にくれました。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ga shukudai wo tetsudatte watashi ni kuremashita.
examples.en: My friend helped me with my homework.
examples.promptEn: State that my friend helped you with your homework and gave it to you using 〜が私にくれます

examples.jp: お母さんがお弁当を作って私にくれました。
examples.romaji: Okaasan ga obentou wo tsukutte watashi ni kuremashita.
examples.en: My mom made me a lunch box.
examples.promptEn: State that my mom made a bento and gave it to you using 〜が私にくれます

examples.jp: 先生がアドバイスを私にくれました。
examples.romaji: Sensei ga adobaisu wo watashi ni kuremashita.
examples.en: The teacher gave me advice.
examples.promptEn: State that my teacher gave you some advice using 〜が私にくれます

title: ～けど、～ (〜kedo、～)
short_explanation: Used to connect two clauses; 'but', 'however', 'although'
long_explanation: The ～けど grammar point is used to connect two clauses, often to show a contrast or to introduce a different point of view. It can be translated as 'but', 'however', or 'although' in English. It's more casual than けれど or が.
formation: Verb-casual + けど / い-adjective + けど / な-adjective + だけど / Noun + だけど

examples.jp: 授業に出たけど、まだ宿題をしないといけない。
examples.romaji: Jugyou ni deta kedo, mada shukudai wo shinai to ikenai.
examples.en: I attended the class, but I still have to do my homework.
examples.promptEn: State that you went to class, but you still have to do your homework using contrast 〜けど

examples.jp: 昨日寒かったけど、今日は暖かいです。
examples.romaji: Kinou samukatta kedo, kyou wa atatakai desu.
examples.en: Yesterday was cold, but today is warm.
examples.promptEn: State that it was cold yesterday, but it's warm today using contrast 〜けど

examples.jp: 彼は親切だけど、ちょっと怖い。
examples.romaji: Kare wa shinsetsu da kedo, chotto kowai.
examples.en: He is kind, but a little scary.
examples.promptEn: State that he's kind, but a little scary using contrast 〜けど

examples.jp: これはおいしそうだけど、高すぎる。
examples.romaji: Kore wa oishisou da kedo, takasugiru.
examples.en: This looks delicious, but it is too expensive.
examples.promptEn: State that this looks delicious, but it's too expensive using contrast 〜けど

title: ～けれど、～ (〜keredo、～)
short_explanation: Expresses a contrast or contradiction; 'but', 'however', 'even though'.
long_explanation: The ～けれど grammar point is used to express a contrast or contradiction between two statements. It can be translated as 'but', 'however', or 'even though' in English. This grammar point is slightly more formal than けど.
formation: Verb-casual + けれど / い-Adjective + けれど / な-Adjective + だけれど / Noun + だけれど

examples.jp: 今日は寒いけれど、散歩に行きます。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa samui keredo, sanpo ni ikimasu.
examples.en: Even though it's cold today, I'll go for a walk.
examples.promptEn: State that it's cold today, but you are going for a walk using contrast 〜けれど

examples.jp: 彼は親切けれど、少し怖いです。
examples.romaji: Kare wa shinsetsu keredo, sukoshi kowai desu.
examples.en: He is kind, but a little scary.
examples.promptEn: State that he's kind, but a little scary using contrast 〜けれど

examples.jp: この部屋は狭いけれど、明るいです。
examples.romaji: Kono heya wa semai keredo, akarui desu.
examples.en: This room is small, but it's bright.
examples.promptEn: State that this room is small, but it's bright using contrast 〜けれど

examples.jp: 彼女は病気だけれど、毎日働いています。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa byouki dakeredo, mainichi hataraite imasu.
examples.en: She is sick, but she works every day.
examples.promptEn: State that she is sick, but she works every day using contrast 〜けれど

title: こちら～ (kochira～)
short_explanation: Refers to a person, place or thing; 'this', 'this one', 'this way', 'here'.
long_explanation: The こちら grammar point is used to refer to a person, place, or thing that is closer to the speaker, or to show politeness when referring to someone. It can mean 'this', 'this one', 'this way', or 'here'.
formation: こちら / こちら + の + Person/Thing

examples.jp: こちらは田中さんです。
examples.romaji: Kochira wa Tanaka-san desu.
examples.en: This is Mr./Ms. Tanaka.
examples.promptEn: State that this is Mr. Tanaka using 〜こちら

examples.jp: こちらのレストランは美味しいです。
examples.romaji: Kochira no resutoran wa oishii desu.
examples.en: This restaurant is delicious.
examples.promptEn: State that this restaurant serves delicious food using 〜こちら

examples.jp: こちらへどうぞ。
examples.romaji: Kochira e douzo.
examples.en: Please come this way.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to click here using 〜こちら

examples.jp: こちらの方がいいですか、それともあちらの方がいいですか？
examples.romaji: Kochira no hou ga ii desu ka, sore to mo achira no hou ga ii desu ka?
examples.en: Is this one better, or is that one better?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether is this one better, or is that one better using 〜こちら

title: さっき～ (sakki～)
short_explanation: Refers to a short time ago or just now.
long_explanation: The word さっき (sakki) is an adverb used to express that something happened or was done a short time ago or just now. It can be combined with verbs or other phrases to convey that meaning.
formation: さっき + verb / さっき + phrase

examples.jp: さっき電話がありました。
examples.romaji: Sakki denwa ga arimashita.
examples.en: There was a phone call just now.
examples.promptEn: State that you just got a phone call using limitation 〜さっき

examples.jp: さっき部屋を掃除しました。
examples.romaji: Sakki heya wo souji shimashita.
examples.en: I cleaned the room a short while ago.
examples.promptEn: State that you cleaned your room a little while ago using limitation 〜さっき

examples.jp: さっき彼に会いました。
examples.romaji: Sakki kare ni aimashita.
examples.en: I met him just now.
examples.promptEn: State that you just saw him using limitation 〜さっき

examples.jp: さっきのニュースを見ましたか？
examples.romaji: Sakki no nyuusu wo mimashita ka?
examples.en: Did you watch the news a short time ago?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether did you see that news story just now using limitation 〜さっき

title: すぐに～ (sugu ni～)
short_explanation: Immediately or right away; used to express promptness or quickness.
long_explanation: The すぐに～ grammar point is used to express an action happening immediately or right away. It often indicates promptness or quickness and can be used with both verbs and adjectives.
formation: すぐに + Verb/Adjective

examples.jp: 友達が来たら、すぐに電話をかけてください。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ga kitara, sugu ni denwa wo kakete kudasai.
examples.en: When my friend arrives, please call me right away.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to if a friend comes over, please call you right away using 〜すぐに

examples.jp: そのニュースを聞いたら、すぐに会社に行きました。
examples.romaji: Sono nyuusu wo kiitara, sugu ni kaisha ni ikimashita.
examples.en: Upon hearing that news, I went to the company immediately.
examples.promptEn: State that as soon as you heard the news, you went straight to the office using 〜すぐに

examples.jp: 彼女はすぐに泣き出した。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa sugu ni nakidashita.
examples.en: She started crying right away.
examples.promptEn: State that she immediately started crying using 〜すぐに

examples.jp: 教室に入ると、先生はすぐに授業を始めた。
examples.romaji: Kyoushitsu ni hairu to, sensei wa sugu ni jugyou wo hajimeta.
examples.en: As soon as I entered the classroom, the teacher started the lesson immediately.
examples.promptEn: State that as soon as you entered the classroom, the teacher began the lesson using 〜すぐに

title: ぜんぜん～ (zenzen～)
short_explanation: Used to express 'not at all' or 'completely' in negative sentences.
long_explanation: The ぜんぜん grammar point is used to emphasize a negative statement and can be translated as 'not at all' or 'completely (in negative sense)'. It is commonly used with negative verbs or negative forms of adjectives, placed before the negative part.
formation: ぜんぜん + [Negative verb/adjective]

examples.jp: 彼はぜんぜん話さない。
examples.romaji: Kare wa zenzen hanasanai.
examples.en: He doesn't talk at all.
examples.promptEn: State that he doesn't talk at all using 〜ぜんぜん

examples.jp: この部屋はぜんぜん暗くない。
examples.romaji: Kono heya wa zenzen kurakunai.
examples.en: This room is not dark at all.
examples.promptEn: State that this room isn't dark at all using 〜ぜんぜん

examples.jp: 彼女はぜんぜん疲れていない。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa zenzen tsukarete inai.
examples.en: She is not tired at all.
examples.promptEn: State that she isn't tired at all using 〜ぜんぜん

examples.jp: その映画はぜんぜん面白くなかった。
examples.romaji: Sono eiga wa zenzen omoshirokunakatta.
examples.en: That movie was not interesting at all.
examples.promptEn: State that that movie wasn't interesting at all using 〜ぜんぜん

title: そして、～ (soshite、～)
short_explanation: Used to connect two sentences; 'and then', 'and'.
long_explanation: The そして grammar point is used to connect two sentences or ideas, expressing a sequence of events or actions. It is commonly translated to 'and then' or simply 'and' in English.
formation: Sentence 1 + そして + Sentence 2

examples.jp: 朝起きて、そして宿題をしました。
examples.romaji: Asa okite, soshite shukudai wo shimashita.
examples.en: I woke up in the morning and then did my homework.
examples.promptEn: State that you woke up in the morning and did your homework using 〜そして

examples.jp: コーヒーを飲んで、そして新聞を読みました。
examples.romaji: Koohii wo nonde, soshite shinbun wo yomimashita.
examples.en: I drank coffee and then read the newspaper.
examples.promptEn: State that you drank some coffee and then read the newspaper using 〜そして

examples.jp: 家を出発しました。そして、駅へ行きました。
examples.romaji: Ie wo shuppatsu shimashita. Soshite, eki e ikimashita.
examples.en: I left my house and then went to the station.
examples.promptEn: State that you left home. Then, you went to the station using 〜そして

examples.jp: 彼はゲームをした。そして、テレビを見ました。
examples.romaji: Kare wa geemu wo shita. Soshite, terebi wo mimashita.
examples.en: He played games and then watched TV.
examples.promptEn: State that he played a game. Then, he watched TV using 〜そして

title: そちら～ (sochira～)
short_explanation: Indicates a direction or person in moderate distance; 'that way', 'that person'.
long_explanation: The そちら grammar point is used to refer to a direction or a person that is moderate distance from both the speaker and listener, often closer to the listener. It can be translated as 'that way', 'that person', or 'that side'. This is distinct from あちら, used for things far from both speaker and listener.
formation: そちら [alone] / そちら + の + Noun

examples.jp: そちらのレストランはどうですか？
examples.romaji: Sochira no resutoran wa dou desu ka?
examples.en: How is that restaurant over there?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether how about that restaurant using 〜そちら

examples.jp: そちらの方、お名前を教えていただけますか？
examples.romaji: Sochira no kata, onamae o oshiete itadakemasu ka?
examples.en: Could you tell me the name of that person over there?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether could you tell you your name, please using 〜そちら

examples.jp: そちらに行く途中で駅があります。
examples.romaji: Sochira ni iku tochuu de eki ga arimasu.
examples.en: There is a station on the way to that direction.
examples.promptEn: State that there is a station on the way there using 〜そちら

examples.jp: そちらのかばん、私のと似ていますね。
examples.romaji: Sochira no kaban, watashi no to niteimasu ne.
examples.en: That bag over there looks similar to mine.
examples.promptEn: State that that bag of yours looks a lot like yours using 〜そちら

title: それから、～ (sorekara、～)
short_explanation: Meaning 'after that', 'and then' or 'then', indicating sequence of events.
long_explanation: The それから grammar point is used to describe the sequence of events or actions, indicating that one action or event takes place after another. It can be translated as 'after that', 'and then', or 'then' in English. It can be used with verbs, adjectives, and nouns but should be placed between two clauses.
formation: Clause 1 + それから + Clause 2

examples.jp: コーヒーを飲んで、それから家を出ました。
examples.romaji: Koohii o nonde, sorekara ie o demashita.
examples.en: I drank coffee, and then I left the house.
examples.promptEn: State that you drank some coffee, and then you left the house using reason 〜それから

examples.jp: 買い物をして、それから映画を見に行きました。
examples.romaji: Kaimono o shite, sorekara eiga o mini ikimashita.
examples.en: I went shopping, and then I went to watch a movie.
examples.promptEn: State that you went shopping, and then you went to see a movie using reason 〜それから

examples.jp: 彼女は勉強をして、それから寝ました。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa benkyou o shite, sorekara nemashita.
examples.en: She studied, and then she went to sleep.
examples.promptEn: State that she studied, and then went to sleep using reason 〜それから

examples.jp: パーティーに行って、それから友達と話しました。
examples.romaji: Paatii ni itte, sorekara tomodachi to hanashimashita.
examples.en: I went to the party, and then I talked with my friends.
examples.promptEn: State that you went to a party, and then you talked with your friends using reason 〜それから

title: だいたい〜 (daitai〜)
short_explanation: Expresses 'roughly', 'approximately', or 'almost'.
long_explanation: The だいたい〜 (daitai〜) grammar point is used to express a rough estimate or generalization, meaning 'roughly', 'approximately', or 'almost' in English. It can be used before numbers, amounts, or percentages to show that the value is not exact.
formation: だいたい + Number/Amount/Percentage

examples.jp: だいたい１００人がパーティーに参加しました。
examples.romaji: Daitai hyaku-nin ga paatii ni sanka shimashita.
examples.en: Approximately 100 people attended the party.
examples.promptEn: State that about 100 people attended the party using desire 〜だいたい〜

examples.jp: 彼女はだいたい２時間でその仕事を終えます。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa daitai ni-jikan de sono shigoto o oemasu.
examples.en: She finishes that work in roughly two hours.
examples.promptEn: State that she usually finishes that job in about two hours using desire 〜だいたい〜

examples.jp: だいたい８０％の生徒が試験に合格しました。
examples.romaji: Daitai hachijuu-paasento no seito ga shiken ni goukaku shimashita.
examples.en: About 80% of the students passed the exam.
examples.promptEn: State that about 80% of the students passed the exam using desire 〜だいたい〜

examples.jp: 今日はだいたい３０度の暑さです。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa daitai sanjuu-do no atsusa desu.
examples.en: Today is almost 30 degrees hot.
examples.promptEn: State that it's about 30 degrees today using desire 〜だいたい〜

title: たいてい～ (taitei～)
short_explanation: Used for expressing 'usually', 'mostly', or 'generally'.
long_explanation: The たいてい grammar point is used to describe a situation that occurs frequently or under normal circumstances. It can be translated as 'usually', 'mostly', or 'generally' in English. It is often used with verbs, but can also be used with adjectives and nouns.
formation: たいてい + Verb/い-Adjective/な-Adjective/Noun

examples.jp: たいてい朝８時に起きます。
examples.romaji: Taitei asa hachi-ji ni okimasu.
examples.en: I usually wake up at 8 o'clock in the morning.
examples.promptEn: State that you usually wake up at 8:00 a.m using desire 〜たいてい

examples.jp: 彼はたいてい遅刻します。
examples.romaji: Kare wa taitei chikoku shimasu.
examples.en: He is usually late.
examples.promptEn: State that he is usually late using desire 〜たいてい

examples.jp: この店の商品はたいてい安いです。
examples.romaji: Kono mise no shouhin wa taitei yasui desu.
examples.en: The items at this store are usually cheap.
examples.promptEn: State that the items at this store are usually inexpensive using desire 〜たいてい

examples.jp: たいていの人はその映画が好きです。
examples.romaji: Taitei no hito wa sono eiga ga suki desu.
examples.en: Most people like that movie.
examples.promptEn: State that most people like that movie using desire 〜たいてい

title: だから、～ (dakara、～)
short_explanation: Expresses a reason or cause; 'because', 'so', 'therefore'.
long_explanation: The だから grammar point is used to connect two sentences and express a reason or cause for the second sentence. It is typically used with nouns or な-adjectives, and can be translated as 'because', 'so', or 'therefore' in English. For verbs/い-adjectives, the form is usually ～から (not だから).
formation: Noun + だから / な-Adjective + だから

examples.jp: 雨だから、傘を持って行きましょう。
examples.romaji: Ame dakara, kasa wo motte ikimashou.
examples.en: Because it's raining, let's bring an umbrella.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you it's raining, so let's take an umbrella using reason 〜だから

examples.jp: このケーキは有名だから、みんなが食べたいです。
examples.romaji: Kono keeki wa yuumei dakara, minna ga tabetai desu.
examples.en: Because this cake is famous, everyone wants to eat it.
examples.promptEn: State that this cake is famous, so everyone wants to eat it using reason 〜だから

examples.jp: 彼は病気だから、学校に行けません。
examples.romaji: Kare wa byouki dakara, gakkou ni ikemasen.
examples.en: Because he is sick, he cannot go to school.
examples.promptEn: State that he can't go to school because he's sick using reason 〜だから

examples.jp: 彼女は学生だから、このレストランで割引があります。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa gakusei dakara, kono resutoran de waribiki ga arimasu.
examples.en: Because she is a student, there is a discount at this restaurant.
examples.promptEn: State that since she is a student, she gets a discount at this restaurant using reason 〜だから

title: ～たり、～たり します (〜tari, 〜tari shimasu)
short_explanation: Used to list multiple actions or states; 'do things like', 'and'.
long_explanation: The ～たり、～たり します grammar point is used to list multiple actions or states without fully enumerating them. It can imply that there are more items in the list and can be translated as 'do things like', 'and', 'among other things', or 'and so on' in English. It is formed by attaching たり to the casual past tense of the verb, followed by します.
formation: Verb-casual-past + たり + Verb-casual-past + たり + します

examples.jp: 休日には、映画を見たり、友達と遊んだりします。
examples.romaji: Kyuujitsu ni wa, eiga wo mitari, tomodachi to asondari shimasu.
examples.en: On holidays, I do things like watch movies and hang out with friends.
examples.promptEn: State that on your days off, you watch movies and hang out with friends using listing 〜たり～たりします

examples.jp: 彼は歌ったり、踊ったり、ピアノを弾いたりします。
examples.romaji: Kare wa utattari, odottari, piano wo hikitari shimasu.
examples.en: He sings, dances, plays the piano, among other things.
examples.promptEn: State that he sings, dances, and plays the piano using listing 〜たり～たりします

examples.jp: このレストランでは、寿司を食べたり、刺身を食べたりします。
examples.romaji: Kono resutoran de wa, sushi wo tabetari, sashimi wo tabetari shimasu.
examples.en: At this restaurant, you can eat sushi, sashimi, and so on.
examples.promptEn: State that at this restaurant, you can eat sushi or sashimi using listing 〜たり～たりします

examples.jp: 彼女は毎朝、ジョギングしたり、ヨガをしたりします。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa maiasa, joggingu shitari, yoga wo shitari shimasu.
examples.en: Every morning, she does things like jogging and yoga.
examples.promptEn: State that she goes jogging or does yoga every morning using listing 〜たり～たりします

title: だれ～ (dare～)
short_explanation: Asking 'who' in a sentence, used to inquire about someone's identity or to clarify who is being referred to.
long_explanation: The だれ〜 grammar point is used to ask about the identity of someone in a sentence. It can be translated as 'who' or 'whom' in English. It is often used with the particle が, は, or を, but can also be combined with other particles depending on the context.
formation: だれ + appropriate particle (が, は or を)

examples.jp: だれがその本を買いましたか。
examples.romaji: Dare ga sono hon o kaimashita ka.
examples.en: Who bought that book?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether who bought that book using 〜だれ

examples.jp: だれを待っていますか。
examples.romaji: Dare o matteimasu ka.
examples.en: Whom are you waiting for?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether who are you waiting for using 〜だれ

examples.jp: だれがそのリンゴを食べましたか。
examples.romaji: Dare ga sono ringo o tabemashita ka.
examples.en: Who ate that apple?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether who ate that apple using 〜だれ

examples.jp: だれが鍵を持っていますか。
examples.romaji: Dare ga kagi o motteimasu ka.
examples.en: Who has the key?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether who has the key using 〜だれ

title: だれか〜 (dareka〜)
short_explanation: Indicates 'someone' or something done or possessed by 'someone'.
long_explanation: The grammar point だれか〜 is used to suggest that something is done by, possessed by, or related to 'someone', usually when the actual person is unidentified or not important. It can be used with verbs, adjectives, or nouns.
formation: だれか + Verb, だれか + Adjective, だれか + Noun

examples.jp: だれかがドアをノックしました。
examples.romaji: Dareka ga doa wo nokku shimashita.
examples.en: Someone knocked on the door.
examples.promptEn: State that someone knocked on the door using 〜だれか〜

examples.jp: だれかが私の傘を盗みました。
examples.romaji: Dareka ga watashi no kasa wo nusumimashita.
examples.en: Someone stole my umbrella.
examples.promptEn: State that someone stole your umbrella using 〜だれか〜

examples.jp: だれか助けてください。
examples.romaji: Dareka tasukete kudasai.
examples.en: Someone, please help.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to help you using 〜だれか〜

examples.jp: だれかのせいで、電気がきれました。
examples.romaji: Dareka no sei de, denki ga kiremashita.
examples.en: Because of someone, the electricity went out.
examples.promptEn: State that someone caused the power to go out using 〜だれか〜

title: だれでも～ (dare demo～)
short_explanation: Used to express 'anyone' or 'everyone'; 'no matter who'.
long_explanation: The grammar point だれでも is used to emphasize that something applies to everyone or anyone, regardless of who they are. It can be translated as 'anyone', 'everyone', or 'no matter who' in English. It is used in sentences to show that a certain situation, characteristic, or condition applies to all people.
formation: だれでも + Verb/Adjective/Noun

examples.jp: だれでもこのゲームができます。
examples.romaji: Dare demo kono geemu ga dekimasu.
examples.en: Anyone can play this game.
examples.promptEn: State that anyone can play this game using contrast 〜だれでも

examples.jp: だれでも疲れることがあります。
examples.romaji: Dare demo tsukareru koto ga arimasu.
examples.en: Everyone gets tired sometimes.
examples.promptEn: State that everyone gets tired sometimes using contrast 〜だれでも

examples.jp: だれでも無料でこのイベントに参加できます。
examples.romaji: Dare demo muryou de kono ibento ni sanka dekimasu.
examples.en: Anyone can participate in this event for free.
examples.promptEn: State that anyone can participate in this event for free using contrast 〜だれでも

examples.jp: だれでもこの町の観光スポットを楽しむことができます。
examples.romaji: Dare demo kono machi no kankou supotto wo tanoshimu koto ga dekimasu.
examples.en: No matter who you are, you can enjoy the sightseeing spots in this town.
examples.promptEn: State that anyone can enjoy the tourist attractions in this town using contrast 〜だれでも

title: だれも～ないです (dare mo ~ nai desu)
short_explanation: Express 'nobody' or 'no one' in a negative sentence.
long_explanation: The grammar point だれも～ないです is used to express the idea of 'nobody' or 'no one' in a negative sentence. だれも is followed by the negative form of a verb or adjective, often using the polite ないです form.
formation: だれも + Verb-negative form (ないです), だれも + い-Adjective-negative form (ないです), だれも + な-Adjective-negative form (じゃないです)

examples.jp: だれも知らないです。
examples.romaji: Daremo shiranai desu.
examples.en: Nobody knows.
examples.promptEn: State that no one knows using 〜だれも～ないです

examples.jp: だれも来ないです。
examples.romaji: Daremo konai desu.
examples.en: Nobody is coming.
examples.promptEn: State that no one is coming using 〜だれも～ないです

examples.jp: 彼女はだれも好きじゃないです。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa daremo suki ja nai desu.
examples.en: She doesn't like anyone.
examples.promptEn: State that she doesn't like anyone using 〜だれも～ないです

examples.jp: ここにはだれもいないです。
examples.romaji: Koko ni wa daremo inai desu.
examples.en: There is nobody here.
examples.promptEn: State that there's no one here using 〜だれも～ないです

title: だれも～ません (daremo ~masen)
short_explanation: Express 'nobody' or 'no one' in negative sentences.
long_explanation: The grammar point だれも is used in combination with a negative form of the verb, usually ません, to express the idea of 'nobody' or 'no one' doing something. It is used with questions or statements and can be translated as 'nobody' or 'no one' in English.
formation: だれも + Verb-negative (ません)

examples.jp: だれも秘密を知りません。
examples.romaji: Daremo himitsu wo shirimasen.
examples.en: No one knows the secret.
examples.promptEn: State that no one knows the secret using 〜だれも～ません

examples.jp: だれもその質問に答えませんでした。
examples.romaji: Daremo sono shitsumon ni kotaemasen deshita.
examples.en: Nobody answered that question.
examples.promptEn: State that no one answered that question using 〜だれも～ません

examples.jp: だれも彼を助けてあげません。
examples.romaji: Daremo kare wo tasukete agemasen.
examples.en: Nobody will help him.
examples.promptEn: State that no one helps him using 〜だれも～ません

examples.jp: だれもその映画を見たがりません。
examples.romaji: Daremo sono eiga wo mitagarimasen.
examples.en: No one wants to watch that movie.
examples.promptEn: State that no one wants to watch that movie using 〜だれも～ません

title: ～どう しますか。 (～dou shimasu ka.)
short_explanation: Asking for someone's opinion or decision; 'what will you do?', 'how will you handle it?'.
long_explanation: The ～どうしますか grammar point is used to ask for someone's opinion, decision, or course of action in a specific situation. It can be translated as 'what will you do?' or 'how will you handle it?' in English. This grammar point is formed by attaching どうしますか to the end of a sentence.
formation: Situation + どうしますか

examples.jp: 雨が降っているので、どうしますか？
examples.romaji: Ame ga futte iru node, dou shimasu ka?
examples.en: It's raining, so what will you do?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether it's raining. What should you do using 〜どうしますか

examples.jp: この問題について、どうしますか？
examples.romaji: Kono mondai ni tsuite, dou shimasu ka?
examples.en: What are you going to do about this issue?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether how would you approach this problem using 〜どうしますか

examples.jp: 彼が来なかったら、どうしますか？
examples.romaji: Kare ga konakattara, dou shimasu ka?
examples.en: If he doesn't come, what will you do?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether what will you do if he doesn't come using 〜どうしますか

examples.jp: 進路を決める時、どうしますか？
examples.romaji: Shinro wo kimeru toki, dou shimasu ka?
examples.en: What will you do when choosing your career path?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether what do you do when deciding on a career path using 〜どうしますか

title: ～どうですか。 (〜dou desu ka.)
short_explanation: Asking for opinions or suggestions; 'how about', 'what do you think of'.
long_explanation: The ～どうですか grammar point is used to ask for someone's opinion or suggestion on something. It can be translated as 'how about' or 'what do you think of' in English. This expression is neither casual nor super-formal, and can be used in various situations.
formation: Noun + は/が + どうですか / Verb-casual + の + どうですか / い-Adjective + どうですか / な-Adjective + な + どうですか

examples.jp: この映画はどうですか？
examples.romaji: Kono eiga wa dou desu ka?
examples.en: How about this movie? / What do you think of this movie?
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you what do you think of this movie? using suggestion 〜どうですか

examples.jp: 晩ご飯に寿司を食べるのはどうですか？
examples.romaji: Bangohan ni sushi wo taberu no wa dou desu ka?
examples.en: How about eating sushi for dinner?
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you how about having sushi for dinner? using suggestion 〜どうですか

examples.jp: この部屋は広いと思いますが、どうですか？
examples.romaji: Kono heya wa hiroi to omoimasu ga, dou desu ka?
examples.en: I think this room is spacious, what do you think?
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you you think this room is spacious—what do you think? using suggestion 〜どうですか

examples.jp: 新しい会社の要件が厳しいですね。鈴木さん、転職するならどうですか？
examples.romaji: Atarashii kaisha no youken ga kibishii desu ne. Suzuki-san, tenshoku suru nara dou desu ka?
examples.en: The new company's requirements are strict, aren't they? Suzuki-san, how about changing jobs if that's the case?
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you the new company's requirements are pretty strict, aren't they? Mr. Suzuki, how about changing jobs? using suggestion 〜どうですか

title: どうやって～ (douyatte～)
short_explanation: Ask 'how' something is done or how to do something.
long_explanation: The grammar point どうやって is used to ask how something is done or how to do something, and is translated as 'how' in English. It is often used in combination with verbs to inquire about the method or process someone goes through to complete a task or action.
formation: どうやって + Verb-casual

examples.jp: どうやってお寿司を作りますか？
examples.romaji: Douyatte o-sushi wo tsukurimasu ka?
examples.en: How do you make sushi?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether how do you make sushi using 〜どうやって

examples.jp: どうやって日本語を勉強しましたか？
examples.romaji: Douyatte nihongo wo benkyou shimashita ka?
examples.en: How did you study Japanese?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether how did you study Japanese using 〜どうやって

examples.jp: どうやってこの問題を解決しますか？
examples.romaji: Douyatte kono mondai wo kaiketsu shimasu ka?
examples.en: How do you solve this problem?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether how would you solve this problem using 〜どうやって

examples.jp: どうやって駅に行きますか？
examples.romaji: Douyatte eki ni ikimasu ka?
examples.en: How do you go to the station?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether how do you get to the station using 〜どうやって

title: ～どう 言いますか。 (〜dou iimasu ka.)
short_explanation: Asking for the way to say something; 'how do you say'.
long_explanation: The ～どう言いますか grammar point is used to ask someone how to express something in a particular language or the appropriate way to say it. It can be translated as 'how do you say' in English.
formation: Word/Phrase + は [language]でどう言いますか / Word/Phrase + をどう言いますか

examples.jp: 「ありがとう」は英語でどう言いますか。
examples.romaji: 「Arigatou」wa eigo de dou iimasu ka.
examples.en: How do you say 'thank you' in English?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether how do you say "Thank you" in English using 〜どう言いますか

examples.jp: この言葉を日本語でどう言いますか。
examples.romaji: Kono kotoba wo nihongo de dou iimasu ka.
examples.en: How do you say this word in Japanese?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether how do you say this in Japanese using 〜どう言いますか

examples.jp: 「すみません」はフランス語でどう言いますか。
examples.romaji: 「Sumimasen」wa furansugo de dou iimasu ka.
examples.en: How do you say 'excuse me' in French?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether how do you say "Excuse you" in French using 〜どう言いますか

examples.jp: その表現をスペイン語でどう言いますか。
examples.romaji: Sono hyougen wo supeingo de dou iimasu ka.
examples.en: How do you say that expression in Spanish?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether how would you say that in Spanish using 〜どう言いますか

title: ～とき (〜toki)
short_explanation: Expresses the time when something happens, 'when', 'at the time'.
long_explanation: The ～とき grammar point is used to express the time when something happens or happened. It can be translated as 'when' or 'at the time' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
formation: Verb-casual + とき / い-Adjective + とき / な-Adjective + なとき / Noun + のとき

examples.jp: 公園で遊ぶとき、帽子をかぶりましょう。
examples.romaji: Kouen de asobu toki, boushi wo kaburimashou.
examples.en: When playing in the park, let's wear a hat.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you wear hats when you play in the park using 〜とき

examples.jp: このりんごが赤いとき、食べごろです。
examples.romaji: Kono ringo ga akai toki, tabegoro desu.
examples.en: This apple is ready to eat when it is red.
examples.promptEn: Ask whether when this apple is red, it's ready to eat using 〜とき

examples.jp: 私が勉強するとき、家族は静かにしてくれます。
examples.romaji: Watashi ga benkyou suru toki, kazoku wa shizuka ni shite kuremasu.
examples.en: When I am studying, my family keeps quiet for me.
examples.promptEn: Politely ask someone to when you study, your family keeps it quiet using 〜とき

examples.jp: 子供のとき、よくおばあちゃんの家に遊びに行きました。
examples.romaji: Kodomo no toki, yoku obaachan no ie ni asobi ni ikimashita.
examples.en: When I was a child, I often went to play at my grandmother's house.
examples.promptEn: Ask whether when you was a child, you often went to your grandmother's house to play using 〜とき

title: ときどき～ (tokidoki～)
short_explanation: Used to indicate the frequency of an event; 'sometimes', 'occasionally', 'now and then'.
long_explanation: The grammar point ときどき is an adverb used to describe an event or action that occurs occasionally or at irregular intervals. It can be translated as 'sometimes', 'occasionally', or 'now and then' in English. It is often used to indicate that the speaker cannot predict the exact time when a certain event occurs.
formation: ときどき + Verb/Adjective/Noun

examples.jp: 彼はときどきケーキを作ります。
examples.romaji: Kare wa tokidoki keeki o tsukurimasu.
examples.en: He sometimes makes cakes.
examples.promptEn: State that he bakes cakes from time to time using 〜ときどき

examples.jp: ときどき雨が降るので、傘を持って行ったほうがいいです。
examples.romaji: Tokidoki ame ga furu node, kasa o motte itta hou ga ii desu.
examples.en: It occasionally rains, so it's better to bring an umbrella.
examples.promptEn: State that it rains from time to time, so you should bring an umbrella using 〜ときどき

examples.jp: 私はときどきこの店で買い物をします。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa tokidoki kono mise de kaimono o shimasu.
examples.en: I shop at this store now and then.
examples.promptEn: State that you shop at this store from time to time using 〜ときどき

examples.jp: 彼女はときどき遅刻します。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa tokidoki chikoku shimasu.
examples.en: She is sometimes late.
examples.promptEn: State that she is sometimes late using 〜ときどき

title: どこ～ (doko～)
short_explanation: Express 'where', used with question words for asking about locations.
long_explanation: The どこ～ grammar point is used to express 'where', primarily for asking about locations or places. It is often combined with question words such as どこへ (doko e), どこで (doko de), and どこに (doko ni) to ask about destinations, locations of actions, and existence, respectively.
formation: どこ + question particle

examples.jp: 駅はどこですか？
examples.romaji: Eki wa doko desu ka?

examples.promptEn: Ask whether how old are you using 〜なん

examples.jp: これはなんですか？
examples.romaji: Kore wa nan desu ka?
examples.en: What is this?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether what is this using 〜なん

examples.jp: 彼はなんで来ましたか？
examples.romaji: Kare wa nan de kimashita ka?
examples.en: Why did he come?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether why did he come using 〜なん

examples.jp: あのレストランはなんと言う名前ですか？
examples.romaji: Ano resutoran wa nan to iu namae desu ka?
examples.en: What is the name of that restaurant?

title: なんで～ (nande～)
short_explanation: Asking the reason or cause; 'why', 'how come'.
long_explanation: The なんで grammar point is used to ask the reason or cause behind something. It can be translated as 'why' or 'how come' in English. It is a casual way of asking for an explanation, and it can be used with verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives, and nouns.
formation: なんで + [phrase or sentence]

examples.jp: なんで遅れたの？
examples.romaji: Nande okureta no?
examples.en: Why were you late?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether why were you late using reason 〜なんで

examples.jp: なんでこの部屋はこんなに汚いの？
examples.romaji: Nande kono heya wa konna ni kitanai no?
examples.en: Why is this room so dirty?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether why is this room so messy using reason 〜なんで

examples.jp: なんで彼女は怒っているの？
examples.romaji: Nande kanojo wa okotte iru no?
examples.en: Why is she angry?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether why is she angry using reason 〜なんで

examples.jp: なんで今日は休みなの？
examples.romaji: Nande kyou wa yasumi na no?
examples.en: Why is today a holiday?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether why do you have the day off today using reason 〜なんで

title: なんでも～ (nandemo～)
short_explanation: Means 'any', 'anything', 'anyone'.
long_explanation: The なんでも grammar point is used to express the concept of 'any', 'anything', or 'anyone' in Japanese. It can be used with verbs, adjectives, and nouns. It is often used in the meaning of 'no matter what' or 'regardless of'.
formation: なんでも + Verb / なんでも + Adjective / なんでも + Noun

examples.jp: なんでも食べられるから、何を頼んでも大丈夫です。
examples.romaji: Nandemo taberareru kara, nani wo tanondemo daijoubu desu.
examples.en: I can eat anything, so it's okay to order whatever you want.
examples.promptEn: State that you can eat anything, so it's fine to order whatever you like using contrast 〜なんでも

examples.jp: なんでもよければ、この本をおすすめします。
examples.romaji: Nandemo yokereba, kono hon wo osusume shimasu.
examples.en: If you're okay with anything, I recommend this book.
examples.promptEn: State that if you're looking for a book, you recommend this one using contrast 〜なんでも

examples.jp: なんでもできるスタッフを探しています。
examples.romaji: Nandemo dekiru sutaffu wo sagashiteimasu.
examples.en: We are looking for a staff member who can do anything.
examples.promptEn: State that we are looking for staff who can do anything using contrast 〜なんでも

examples.jp: この食堂では、なんでも美味しくて安い料理が出されます。
examples.romaji: Kono shokudou de wa, nandemo oishikute yasui ryouri ga dasaremasu.
examples.en: In this cafeteria, any dish served is delicious and inexpensive.
examples.promptEn: State that this cafeteria serves delicious and inexpensive food using contrast 〜なんでも

title: ～なんと 言いますか。 (〜nan to iimasu ka.)
short_explanation: Asking how something is called or referred to; 'how do you say'
long_explanation: The ～なんと言いますか grammar point is used to ask how something is called, expressed, or referred to in a polite manner. It can be translated as 'how do you say' or 'what do you call' in English. The formation is used with a noun or a topic where you would like to know the proper expression or name for something.
formation: Noun + は/が + なんと言いますか

examples.jp: この花はなんと言いますか。
examples.romaji: Kono hana wa nan to iimasu ka.
examples.en: How do you say this flower?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether what is this flower called using 〜なんと言いますか

examples.jp: この料理はなんと言いますか。
examples.romaji: Kono ryouri wa nan to iimasu ka.
examples.en: What do you call this dish?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether what is this dish called using 〜なんと言いますか

examples.jp: 日本でこれはなんと言いますか。
examples.romaji: Nihon de kore wa nan to iimasu ka.
examples.en: How do you say this in Japanese?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether how do you say this in Japanese using 〜なんと言いますか

examples.jp: その映画の名前はなんと言いますか。
examples.romaji: Sono eiga no namae wa nan to iimasu ka.
examples.en: What is the name of that movie?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether what is the name of that movie using 〜なんと言いますか

title: ～に あげます (〜 ni agemasu)
short_explanation: Used to express giving something to someone; 'give', 'offer'.
long_explanation: The ～に あげます grammar point is used when the speaker offers or gives something to someone. It emphasizes that the action is performed for the benefit of the receiver. The formation involves using the particle 'に' after the person receiving the item, followed by the verb あげます.
formation: Receiver + に + Object + を + あげます

examples.jp: 私は友達に本をあげました。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa tomodachi ni hon wo agemashita.
examples.en: I gave a book to my friend.
examples.promptEn: State that you gave a book to your friend using giving and receiving 〜にあげます

examples.jp: 彼にプレゼントをあげましょう。
examples.romaji: Kare ni purezento wo agemashou.
examples.en: Let's give him a present.
examples.promptEn: Suggest that you give him a present using giving and receiving 〜にあげます

examples.jp: 先生に花をあげます。
examples.romaji: Sensei ni hana wo agemasu.
examples.en: I will give flowers to the teacher.
examples.promptEn: State that you are going to give the teacher some flowers using giving and receiving 〜にあげます

examples.jp: お母さんにチョコレートをあげたいです。
examples.romaji: Okaasan ni chokoreeto wo agetai desu.
examples.en: I want to give chocolate to my mom.
examples.promptEn: State that you want to give your mom some chocolate using giving and receiving 〜にあげます

title: ～に もらいます (〜ni moraimasu)
short_explanation: To receive something or some action from someone; 'to get', 'to receive'.
long_explanation: The ～に もらいます grammar point is used to express receiving something or some action from someone. It can be translated as 'to get' or 'to receive' in English. The formation involves placing に after the giver and もらいます to show the act of receiving.
formation: Giver + に + Verb-te form + もらいます / Giver + に + Object + を + もらいます

examples.jp: 友達にプレゼントをもらいました。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ni purezento wo moraimashita.
examples.en: I received a gift from my friend.
examples.promptEn: State that you received a gift from a friend using 〜にもらいます

examples.jp: 先生にアドバイスをもらいました。
examples.romaji: Sensei ni adobaisu wo moraimashita.
examples.en: I got advice from my teacher.
examples.promptEn: State that you received some advice from your teacher using 〜にもらいます

examples.jp: おばあさんに手紙を書いてもらいました。
examples.romaji: Obaasan ni tegami wo kaite moraimashita.
examples.en: I had my grandmother write a letter for me.
examples.promptEn: State that my grandmother wrote a letter for you using 〜にもらいます

examples.jp: 弟に宿題を手伝ってもらいました。
examples.romaji: Otouto ni shukudai wo tetsudatte moraimashita.
examples.en: I got help from my younger brother with my homework.
examples.promptEn: State that my younger brother helped you with your homework using 〜にもらいます

title: ～の (〜no)
short_explanation: Express possession, apposition, or description using 'of' or ''s'.
long_explanation: The ～の grammar point is used to express possession, apposition, or description. It functions like 'of' or an apostrophe + 's' (’s) in English. It can be used with nouns, adjectives, and verbs to show relationships between words.
formation: Noun1 + の + Noun2, (Adjective/Clause) + の (nominalized), etc.

examples.jp: これは私の鞄です。
examples.romaji: Kore wa watashi no kaban desu.
examples.en: This is my bag.
examples.promptEn: State that this is your bag using 〜の

examples.jp: 彼女は赤いバッグを持っています。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa akai baggu o motte imasu.
examples.en: She has a red bag.
examples.promptEn: State that she has a red bag using 〜の

examples.jp: 彼はきれいな部屋があります。
examples.romaji: Kare wa kirei na heya ga arimasu.
examples.en: He has a clean room.
examples.promptEn: State that he has a clean room using 〜の

examples.jp: 東京の天気は暑いです。
examples.romaji: Toukyou no tenki wa atsui desu.
examples.en: The weather in Tokyo is hot.
examples.promptEn: State that it's hot in Tokyo using 〜の

title: ～はたいへんです (〜wa taihen desu)
short_explanation: Express that something is difficult or tough.
long_explanation: The ～はたいへんです grammar point is used to express that something is difficult or tough to do, handle, or face. It can be translated as 'is difficult' or 'is tough' in English. The formation is used with a noun followed by はたいへんです.
formation: Noun + はたいへんです

examples.jp: 漢字を覚えるのはたいへんです。
examples.romaji: Kanji o oboeru no wa taihen desu.
examples.en: It is difficult to remember kanji.
examples.promptEn: State that learning kanji is hard using desire 〜はたいへんです

examples.jp: この仕事はたいへんです。
examples.romaji: Kono shigoto wa taihen desu.
examples.en: This job is tough.
examples.promptEn: State that this job is tough using desire 〜はたいへんです

examples.jp: 日本の駅のことを理解するのはたいへんです。
examples.romaji: Nihon no eki no koto o rikai suru no wa taihen desu.
examples.en: Understanding Japanese train stations is difficult.
examples.promptEn: State that it's hard to understand Japanese train stations using desire 〜はたいへんです

examples.jp: 彼女は病気の時、生活はたいへんです。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa byouki no toki, seikatsu wa taihen desu.
examples.en: When she is sick, life is tough.
examples.promptEn: Ask whether when she is sick, life is difficult using desire 〜はたいへんです

title: ほとんど〜 (hotondo〜)
short_explanation: Used to express 'almost', 'nearly', or 'most'.
long_explanation: The ほとんど〜 grammar point is used to express that something is 'almost', 'nearly', or 'most'. It can appear in both negative contexts (hardly/barely) or positive contexts (almost all). It is typically followed by a verb or used with a noun to describe the quantity or extent of something.
formation: ほとんど + Verb / ほとんど + Noun

examples.jp: 彼女はほとんど英語を話せません。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa hotondo eigo o hanasemasen.
examples.en: She can hardly speak English.
examples.promptEn: State that she can hardly speak any English using 〜ほとんど〜

examples.jp: ほとんどの人がパーティーに出席しました。
examples.romaji: Hotondo no hito ga paatii ni shusseki shimashita.
examples.en: Most people attended the party.
examples.promptEn: State that most people attended the party using 〜ほとんど〜

examples.jp: 私たちはほとんど勉強しないでテストに合格しました。
examples.romaji: Watashitachi wa hotondo benkyou shinaide tesuto ni goukaku shimashita.
examples.en: We passed the test with hardly any studying.
examples.promptEn: State that we passed the test without studying much using 〜ほとんど〜

examples.jp: この本はほとんど読み終わりました。
examples.romaji: Kono hon wa hotondo yomiowarimashita.
examples.en: I have almost finished reading this book.
examples.promptEn: State that you have almost finished reading this book using 〜ほとんど〜

title: まあまあ～ (maa maa～)
short_explanation: Expresses something as 'so-so', 'not bad', or 'average'.
long_explanation: The expression まあまあ is used to describe something that is neither particularly good nor bad, but rather average or 'so-so'. It is a neutral term and can be used in various contexts when discussing quality, feelings, or situations.
formation: Used as an adverb or short expression with no special grammar structure.

examples.jp: 彼の料理の腕前はまあまあです。
examples.romaji: Kare no ryouri no udemae wa maa maa desu.
examples.en: His cooking skills are so-so.
examples.promptEn: State that his cooking skills are so-so using 〜まあまあ

examples.jp: 今日の天気はまあまあですね。
examples.romaji: Kyou no tenki wa maa maa desu ne.
examples.en: The weather today is not bad, huh?
examples.promptEn: State that the weather today is so-so using 〜まあまあ

examples.jp: あの映画はまあまあ面白かったです。
examples.romaji: Ano eiga wa maa maa omoshirokatta desu.
examples.en: That movie was somewhat interesting.
examples.promptEn: State that that movie was pretty interesting using 〜まあまあ

examples.jp: 彼女の歌はまあまあ上手だと思います。
examples.romaji: Kanojo no uta wa maa maa jouzu da to omoimasu.
examples.en: I think her singing is not bad.
examples.promptEn: State that you think she sings pretty well using 〜まあまあ

title: まだ〜 (mada〜)
short_explanation: Indicates something has not yet happened or is still happening; 'still', 'not yet'.
long_explanation: The まだ〜 grammar point is used to express that something has not yet occurred or is still in progress. It can be translated as 'still' or 'not yet' in English. Depending on the context or if expressing the negative, まだ can be used with different combinations of verb, adjective, or noun.
formation: まだ + Verb (non-past / negative / te-form), まだ + い-adjective, まだ + な-adjective + じゃない/ではない, まだ + Noun + じゃない/ではない

examples.jp: 昼ご飯はまだ食べていません。
examples.romaji: Hirugohan wa mada tabete imasen.
examples.en: I haven't eaten lunch yet.
examples.promptEn: State that you haven't had lunch yet using 〜まだ〜

examples.jp: 山田さんはまだ来ていません。
examples.romaji: Yamada-san wa mada kite imasen.
examples.en: Yamada-san has not arrived yet.
examples.promptEn: State that mr. Yamada hasn't arrived yet using 〜まだ〜

examples.jp: この部屋はまだ暑いです。
examples.romaji: Kono heya wa mada atsui desu.
examples.en: This room is still hot.
examples.promptEn: State that this room is still hot using 〜まだ〜

examples.jp: 彼はまだ学生じゃないです。
examples.romaji: Kare wa mada gakusei ja nai desu.
examples.en: He is not a student yet.
examples.promptEn: State that he is no longer a student using 〜まだ〜

title: まだ〜ないです (mada 〜 nai desu)
short_explanation: Expresses that something has not happened or been done yet.
long_explanation: The まだ〜ないです grammar point is used to indicate that a certain action or event has not yet happened or been completed. It is used with the negative form of a verb (casual negative + です) and can be translated as 'not yet', 'still', or 'haven't' in English.
formation: まだ + Verb-negative + です

examples.jp: まだ宿題をしていないです。
examples.romaji: Mada shukudai o shite inai desu.
examples.en: I haven't done my homework yet.
examples.promptEn: State that you haven't done your homework yet using 〜まだ〜ないです

examples.jp: 彼はまだ来ないです。
examples.romaji: Kare wa mada konai desu.
examples.en: He hasn't come yet.
examples.promptEn: State that he hasn't come yet using 〜まだ〜ないです

examples.jp: 映画はまだ始まっていないです。
examples.romaji: Eiga wa mada hajimatte inai desu.
examples.en: The movie hasn't started yet.
examples.promptEn: State that the movie hasn't started yet using 〜まだ〜ないです

examples.jp: 私たちはまだ夕食を食べていないです。
examples.romaji: Watashitachi wa mada yuushoku o tabete inai desu.
examples.en: We haven't eaten dinner yet.
examples.promptEn: State that we haven't had dinner yet using 〜まだ〜ないです

title: まだ～ません (mada ~masen)
short_explanation: Expresses that something has not happened or been done yet (polite form).
long_explanation: The まだ～ません grammar point is used to express that something has not happened or been done yet in a polite register. It is used with the negative ます-form of a verb (～ません). まだ is placed before the verb phrase.
formation: まだ + Verb-ます form (negative)

examples.jp: 昼ご飯をまだ食べていません。
examples.romaji: Hirugohan o mada tabete imasen.
examples.en: I have not eaten lunch yet.
examples.promptEn: State that you haven't had lunch yet using 〜まだ～ません

examples.jp: 宿題がまだ終わっていません。
examples.romaji: Shukudai ga mada owatte imasen.
examples.en: I have not finished my homework yet.
examples.promptEn: State that you haven't finished your homework yet using 〜まだ～ません

examples.jp: 東京にはまだ行ったことがありません。
examples.romaji: Toukyou ni wa mada itta koto ga arimasen.

examples.promptEn: State that you haven't been to Tokyo yet using 〜まだ～ません

examples.jp: 彼はまだ来ていません。
examples.romaji: Kare wa mada kite imasen.
examples.en: He hasn't come yet.
examples.promptEn: State that he hasn't arrived yet using 〜まだ～ません

title: もう～ (mou～)
short_explanation: Expresses 'already', 'anymore', or 'soon'.
long_explanation: The もう grammar point is used to express the idea of 'already', 'anymore', or 'soon' in English. It indicates that something has already happened, won't happen anymore, or will happen soon. It can be used with verbs, adjectives, or nouns depending on context.
formation: もう + Verb / もう + Adjective / もう + Noun

examples.jp: もう昼ごはんを食べました。
examples.romaji: Mou hirugohan o tabemashita.
examples.en: I already ate lunch.
examples.promptEn: State that you have already had lunch using 〜もう

examples.jp: もうここでは働かない。
examples.romaji: Mou koko de wa hatarakanai.
examples.en: I won't work here anymore.
examples.promptEn: State that you are not working here anymore using 〜もう

examples.jp: もうすぐ夏休みですね。
examples.romaji: Mou sugu natsuyasumi desu ne.
examples.en: Summer vacation is coming soon, isn't it?
examples.promptEn: Ask whether summer vacation is coming up soon, isn't it using 〜もう

examples.jp: もう十分です。
examples.romaji: Mou juubun desu.
examples.en: It's already enough.
examples.promptEn: State that that's enough using 〜もう

title: もうすぐ〜 (mou sugu~)
short_explanation: Express an action or event happening soon: 'soon', 'in a short while', 'almost'.
long_explanation: The もうすぐ grammar point is used to express that an action or event is going to happen soon or is almost happening. It can be translated as 'soon', 'in a short while', or 'almost' in English. もうすぐ is usually followed by a verb or a noun indicating an event.
formation: もうすぐ + Verb (~ます form or 〜る form)

examples.jp: もうすぐ春が来ます。
examples.romaji: Mou sugu haru ga kimasu.
examples.en: Spring is coming soon.
examples.promptEn: State that spring is coming soon using simultaneous action 〜もうすぐ〜

examples.jp: もうすぐ彼女の誕生日です。
examples.romaji: Mou sugu kanojo no tanjoubi desu.
examples.en: Her birthday is coming up soon.
examples.promptEn: State that her birthday is coming up soon using simultaneous action 〜もうすぐ〜

examples.jp: もうすぐ試験が終わる。
examples.romaji: Mou sugu shiken ga owaru.
examples.en: The exam will be over soon.
examples.promptEn: State that the exam is almost over using simultaneous action 〜もうすぐ〜

examples.jp: もうすぐ雨が止むでしょう。
examples.romaji: Mou sugu ame ga yamu deshou.
examples.en: The rain will likely stop soon.
examples.promptEn: State that the rain will probably stop soon using simultaneous action 〜もうすぐ〜

title: もっと〜 (motto〜)
short_explanation: Expresses 'more' or 'even more' when describing a quantity, frequency, or degree.
long_explanation: The もっと〜 grammar point is used to emphasize the desire or need for something to be 'more' or 'even more' in terms of quantity, frequency, or degree. It is often translated as 'more' or 'even more' in English. もっと can be used with verbs, い-adjectives, or な-adjectives.
formation: もっと + Verb / い-Adjective / な-Adjective

examples.jp: もっと勉強しなければなりません。
examples.romaji: Motto benkyou shinakereba narimasen.
examples.en: I have to study more.
examples.promptEn: State that you need to study more using 〜もっと〜

examples.jp: このかばんをもっと大きいサイズに変えたいです。
examples.romaji: Kono kaban o motto ookii saizu ni kaetai desu.
examples.en: I want to change this bag to a larger size.
examples.promptEn: State that you want to switch to a larger size for this bag using 〜もっと〜

examples.jp: もっと静かな場所で働きたいです。
examples.romaji: Motto shizuka na basho de hatarakitai desu.
examples.en: I want to work in a quieter place.
examples.promptEn: State that you want to work in a quieter place using 〜もっと〜

examples.jp: 彼女はもっと上手になりたいと思っています。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa motto jouzu ni naritai to omotte imasu.
examples.en: She wants to become even better.
examples.promptEn: State that she wants to get better at it using 〜もっと〜

title: よく～ (yoku ~)
short_explanation: Often used to express 'doing something well' or 'often'.
long_explanation: The よく～ grammar point is used to express that someone does something well, frequently, or often. It is often placed before the verb and can also mean 'well done' or 'good job' when praising someone's action.
formation: よく + Verb-casual

examples.jp: 彼はよく勉強します。
examples.romaji: Kare wa yoku benkyou shimasu.
examples.en: He studies often.
examples.promptEn: State that he studies hard using 〜よく

examples.jp: 彼女はよく料理を作ります。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa yoku ryouri o tsukurimasu.
examples.en: She often cooks.
examples.promptEn: State that she often cooks using 〜よく

examples.jp: 昔の友達とよく遊んでいました。
examples.romaji: Mukashi no tomodachi to yoku asonde imashita.
examples.en: I used to play a lot with my old friends.
examples.promptEn: State that you used to hang out with your old friends a lot using 〜よく

examples.jp: よくできました！
examples.romaji: Yoku dekimashita!
examples.en: Well done!
examples.promptEn: State that great job using 〜よく

title: ～（場所）に～があります (〜basho ni 〜 ga arimasu)
short_explanation: Express the existence or presence of something in a place.
long_explanation: The ～（場所）に～があります grammar point is used to express the existence or presence of something in a specific location. In this structure, the place is followed by 'に', then the object, plus が, and finally あります (to exist / there is).
formation: Place + に + Object/Thing + が + あります

examples.jp: 図書館にたくさんの本があります。
examples.romaji: Toshokan ni takusan no hon ga arimasu.
examples.en: There are many books in the library.
examples.promptEn: State that there are many books in the library using 〜（場所）に～があります

examples.jp: 公園に池があります。
examples.romaji: Kouen ni ike ga arimasu.
examples.en: There is a pond in the park.
examples.promptEn: State that there is a pond in the park using 〜（場所）に～があります

examples.jp: 駅の前にコンビニがあります。
examples.romaji: Eki no mae ni konbini ga arimasu.
examples.en: There is a convenience store in front of the station.
examples.promptEn: State that there is a convenience store in front of the station using 〜（場所）に～があります

examples.jp: 山の上に神社があります。
examples.romaji: Yama no ue ni jinja ga arimasu.
examples.en: There is a shrine on top of the mountain.
examples.promptEn: State that there is a shrine on top of the mountain using 〜（場所）に～があります
